title: 仲夏夜之夢
author: William Shakespeare 威廉·莎士比亞
description: 《A Midsummer Night’s Dream》(約1595)。雅典附近嘅樹林裡,四個年輕戀人因仙王奧布朗嘅魔法花汁而愛錯人,仙后蒂塔妮婭愛上變咗驢頭嘅織工波頓,一夜荒唐過後,有情人終成眷屬。全劇五幕九場,每段對白標示說話者,英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: Act I, Scene I — Athens. A Room in the Palace of Theseus 第一幕第一場:雅典,忒修斯宮中一室

passages.original: Enter Theseus, Hippolyta, Philostrate and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、菲羅斯特拉特及侍從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、菲羅斯特拉特及侍從上。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Now, fair Hippolyta, our nuptial hour Draws on apace;
passages.vernacular: 而家,美麗嘅希波呂忒,我哋嘅婚禮時刻快到喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,美麗的希波呂忒,我們的婚禮時刻快到了;

passages.original: four happy days bring in Another moon; but oh, methinks, how slow This old moon wanes!
passages.vernacular: 再四個快樂嘅日子就迎嚟另一個月;不過,啊,我覺得呢舊月虧得多慢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再四個快樂的日子就迎來另一個月;可是,啊,我覺得這舊月虧得多慢!

passages.original: She lingers my desires, Like to a step-dame or a dowager, Long withering out a young man’s revenue.
passages.vernacular: 佢拖延咗我嘅慾望,像繼母或寡婦,久久耗住年輕人嘅財產。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它拖延了我的慾望,像繼母或寡婦,久久耗著年輕人的財產。

passages.title: Hippolyta 希波呂忒
passages.original: Four days will quickly steep themselves in night;
passages.vernacular: 四天會好快浸入夜裡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四天會很快浸入夜裡;

passages.original: Four nights will quickly dream away the time;
passages.vernacular: 四個夜晚會好快喺夢中消磨時間;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四個夜晚會很快在夢中消磨時間;

passages.original: And then the moon, like to a silver bow New bent in heaven, shall behold the night Of our solemnities.
passages.vernacular: 然後月亮,像新彎喺天上嘅銀弓,將睇到我哋慶典之夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後月亮,像新彎在天上的銀弓,將看到我們慶典之夜。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Go, Philostrate, Stir up the Athenian youth to merriments;
passages.vernacular: 去,菲羅斯特拉特,激起雅典青年嘅歡樂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,菲羅斯特拉特,激起雅典青年的歡樂;

passages.original: Awake the pert and nimble spirit of mirth; Turn melancholy forth to funerals;
passages.vernacular: 喚醒活潑輕快嘅歡愉精神;把憂鬱趕去葬禮;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喚醒活潑輕快的歡愉精神;把憂鬱趕去葬禮;

passages.original: The pale companion is not for our pomp.
passages.vernacular: 嗰蒼白嘅同伴不適合我哋嘅盛典。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那蒼白的同伴不適合我們的盛典。

passages.original: [Exit Philostrate.]
passages.vernacular: [菲羅斯特拉特下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [菲羅斯特拉特下。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Hippolyta, I woo’d thee with my sword, And won thy love doing thee injuries;
passages.vernacular: 希波呂忒,我用劍向你求愛,以傷害贏得你嘅愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希波呂忒,我用劍向你求愛,以傷害贏得你的愛;

passages.original: But I will wed thee in another key, With pomp, with triumph, and with revelling.
passages.vernacular: 但我將以另一種調子同你成婚,伴住盛典、凱旋同狂歡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我將以另一種調子與你成婚,伴著盛典、凱旋和狂歡。

passages.original: Enter Egeus, Hermia, Lysander and Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: [伊吉斯、赫米婭、拉山德同狄米特律斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [伊吉斯、赫米婭、拉山德與狄米特律斯上。]

passages.title: Egeus 伊吉斯
passages.original: Happy be Theseus, our renownèd Duke!
passages.vernacular: 願我哋著名嘅公爵忒修斯快樂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願我們著名的公爵忒修斯快樂!

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Thanks, good Egeus.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝,好伊吉斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝,好伊吉斯。

passages.original: What’s the news with thee?
passages.vernacular: 你有乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有什麼消息?

passages.title: Egeus 伊吉斯
passages.original: Full of vexation come I, with complaint Against my child, my daughter Hermia.
passages.vernacular: 我滿懷煩惱而嚟,要控訴我嘅細路,我嘅女兒赫米婭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我滿懷煩惱而來,要控訴我的孩子,我的女兒赫米婭。

passages.original: Stand forth, Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: 上前,狄米特律斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上前,狄米特律斯。

passages.original: My noble lord, This man hath my consent to marry her.
passages.vernacular: 我高貴嘅大人,呢個人得到我嘅同意娶佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高貴的大人,這個人得到我的同意娶她。

passages.original: Stand forth, Lysander.
passages.vernacular: 上前,拉山德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上前,拉山德。

passages.original: And, my gracious Duke, This man hath bewitch’d the bosom of my child.
passages.vernacular: 而我仁慈嘅公爵,呢個人迷惑咗我細路嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我仁慈的公爵,這個人迷惑了我孩子的心。

passages.original: Thou, thou, Lysander, thou hast given her rhymes, And interchang’d love-tokens with my child.
passages.vernacular: 你,你,拉山德,你畀佢寫詩,同我嘅細路交換愛情信物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,你,拉山德,你給她寫詩,與我的孩子交換愛情信物。

passages.original: Thou hast by moonlight at her window sung, With feigning voice, verses of feigning love;
passages.vernacular: 你喺月光下喺佢窗前,用假聲唱假意愛情嘅詩;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在月光下在她窗前,用假聲唱假意愛情的詩;

passages.original: And stol’n the impression of her fantasy With bracelets of thy hair, rings, gauds, conceits, Knacks, trifles, nosegays, sweetmeats (messengers Of strong prevailment in unharden’d youth) With cunning hast thou filch’d my daughter’s heart, Turn’d her obedience (which is due to me) To stubborn harshness.
passages.vernacular: 並偷取咗佢幻想嘅印象,用你頭髮做嘅手鐲、戒指、小玩意、巧思、小玩物、無用小物、花束、甜點(呢啲對未變硬嘅青春有強大講服力嘅使者),你用詭計偷咗我女兒嘅心,把佢對我應有嘅服從,變成固執嘅冷酷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並偷取了她幻想的印象,用你頭髮做的手鐲、戒指、小玩意、巧思、小玩物、無用小物、花束、甜點(這些對未變硬的青春有強大說服力的使者),你用詭計偷了我女兒的心,把她對我應有的服從,變成固執的冷酷。

passages.original: And, my gracious Duke, Be it so she will not here before your grace Consent to marry with Demetrius, I beg the ancient privilege of Athens:
passages.vernacular: 而我仁慈嘅公爵,如果佢唔肯喺您面前同意嫁畀狄米特律斯,我請求雅典嘅古老特權:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我仁慈的公爵,如果她不肯在您面前同意嫁給狄米特律斯,我請求雅典的古老特權:

passages.original: As she is mine I may dispose of her; Which shall be either to this gentleman Or to her death, according to our law Immediately provided in that case.
passages.vernacular: 既然佢係我嘅,我可以處置佢;要麼嫁畀呢位紳士,要麼判佢死刑,依我哋嘅法律對此情形立即作出嘅規定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然她是我的,我可以處置她;要麼嫁給這位紳士,要麼判她死刑,依我們的法律對此情形立即作出的規定。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: What say you, Hermia?
passages.vernacular: 你點講,赫米婭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼說,赫米婭?

passages.original: Be advis’d, fair maid.
passages.vernacular: 要聽勸,美麗嘅少女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要聽勸,美麗的少女。

passages.original: To you your father should be as a god; One that compos’d your beauties, yea, and one To whom you are but as a form in wax By him imprinted, and within his power To leave the figure, or disfigure it.
passages.vernacular: 對你來講,你父親應當如同一位神;佢造就咗你嘅美麗,對,你對佢來講就像蠟上被佢印出嘅形狀,佢有權力保留呢形像,或毀壞佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對你來說,你父親應當如同一位神;他造就了你的美麗,對,你對他來說就像蠟上被他印出的形狀,他有權力保留這形像,或毀壞它。

passages.original: Demetrius is a worthy gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 狄米特律斯係位可敬嘅紳士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄米特律斯是位可敬的紳士。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: So is Lysander.
passages.vernacular: 拉山德都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉山德也是。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: In himself he is.
passages.vernacular: 就佢本人而言係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就他本人而言是的。

passages.original: But in this kind, wanting your father’s voice, The other must be held the worthier.
passages.vernacular: 但喺呢件事上,缺少你父親嘅同意,另一位必須被視為更值得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在這件事上,缺少你父親的同意,另一位必須被視為更值得。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: I would my father look’d but with my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 我但願我父親用我嘅眼睛睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我但願我父親用我的眼睛看。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Rather your eyes must with his judgment look.
passages.vernacular: 倒不如你嘅眼睛必須用佢嘅判斷去睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 倒不如你的眼睛必須用他的判斷去看。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: I do entreat your Grace to pardon me.
passages.vernacular: 我懇求您大人原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求您大人原諒我。

passages.original: I know not by what power I am made bold, Nor how it may concern my modesty In such a presence here to plead my thoughts:
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道憑乜嘢力量我變得大膽,都唔知道喺咁樣嘅場合當眾陳述我嘅想法,對我嘅端莊有乜嘢影響:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道憑什麼力量我變得大膽,也不知道在這樣的場合當眾陳述我的想法,對我的端莊有什麼影響:

passages.original: But I beseech your Grace that I may know The worst that may befall me in this case, If I refuse to wed Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: 但我懇求大人,讓我知道喺呢件事上最壞會發生乜嘢,如果我拒絕嫁畀狄米特律斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我懇求大人,讓我知道在這件事上最壞會發生什麼,如果我拒絕嫁給狄米特律斯。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Either to die the death, or to abjure For ever the society of men.
passages.vernacular: 要麼死刑,要麼永遠棄絕同男人嘅交往。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼死刑,要麼永遠棄絕與男人的交往。

passages.original: Therefore, fair Hermia, question your desires, Know of your youth, examine well your blood, Whether, if you yield not to your father’s choice, You can endure the livery of a nun, For aye to be in shady cloister mew’d, To live a barren sister all your life, Chanting faint hymns to the cold fruitless moon.
passages.vernacular: 所以,美麗嘅赫米婭,問問你嘅慾望,了解你嘅青春,仔細檢查你嘅血氣,如果你不順從你父親嘅選擇,你能否忍受修女嘅制服,永遠被關喺陰暗嘅修道院裡,一生做一個不育嘅修女,向冷冷無果嘅月亮吟唱微弱嘅聖歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,美麗的赫米婭,問問你的慾望,了解你的青春,仔細檢查你的血氣,如果你不順從你父親的選擇,你能否忍受修女的制服,永遠被關在陰暗的修道院裡,一生做一個不育的修女,向冷冷無果的月亮吟唱微弱的聖歌。

passages.original: Thrice-blessèd they that master so their blood To undergo such maiden pilgrimage, But earthlier happy is the rose distill’d Than that which, withering on the virgin thorn, Grows, lives, and dies, in single blessedness.
passages.vernacular: 三倍有福嘅人,能如此駕馭自己嘅血氣,承受咁樣嘅處女朝聖,但被提煉嘅玫瑰,比嗰喺處女枝上枯萎、喺單身福氣中生長、生活同死去嘅,喺塵世上更幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三倍有福的人,能如此駕馭自己的血氣,承受這樣的處女朝聖,但被提煉的玫瑰,比那在處女枝上枯萎、在單身福氣中生長、生活和死去的,在塵世上更幸福。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: So will I grow, so live, so die, my lord, Ere I will yield my virgin patent up Unto his lordship, whose unwishèd yoke My soul consents not to give sovereignty.
passages.vernacular: 我就咁樣生長、咁樣活、咁樣死,我嘅大人,都唔願把我嘅處女專利交畀佢大人,佢嗰不受歡迎嘅軛,我嘅靈魂不同意畀佢主權。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就這樣生長、這樣活、這樣死,我的大人,也不願把我的處女專利交給他大人,他那不受歡迎的軛,我的靈魂不同意給他主權。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Take time to pause; and by the next new moon The sealing-day betwixt my love and me For everlasting bond of fellowship, Upon that day either prepare to die For disobedience to your father’s will, Or else to wed Demetrius, as he would, Or on Diana’s altar to protest For aye austerity and single life.
passages.vernacular: 畀自己時間考慮;到下一個新月,都就係我嘅愛人同我永遠結為夥伴關係嘅印證之日,喺嗰天,要麼準備因違背父親意願而死,要麼如佢所願嫁畀狄米特律斯,要麼喺狄安娜嘅祭壇前宣誓永遠嚴守苦修同單身生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給自己時間考慮;到下一個新月,也就是我的愛人與我永遠結為夥伴關係的印證之日,在那天,要麼準備因違背父親意願而死,要麼如他所願嫁給狄米特律斯,要麼在狄安娜的祭壇前宣誓永遠嚴守苦修與單身生活。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Relent, sweet Hermia; and, Lysander, yield Thy crazèd title to my certain right.
passages.vernacular: 軟下嚟吧,甜美嘅赫米婭;拉山德,你嗰有缺陷嘅名分讓畀我確定嘅權利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 軟下來吧,甜美的赫米婭;拉山德,你那有缺陷的名分讓給我確定的權利。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: You have her father’s love, Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: 你有佢父親嘅愛,狄米特律斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有她父親的愛,狄米特律斯。

passages.original: Let me have Hermia’s.
passages.vernacular: 讓我有赫米婭嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我有赫米婭的愛。

passages.original: Do you marry him.
passages.vernacular: 你去娶佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去娶他。

passages.title: Egeus 伊吉斯
passages.original: Scornful Lysander, true, he hath my love; And what is mine my love shall render him;
passages.vernacular: 輕蔑嘅拉山德,不錯,佢有我嘅愛;而我嘅愛將把屬於我嘅畀佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕蔑的拉山德,不錯,他有我的愛;而我的愛將把屬於我的給他;

passages.original: And she is mine, and all my right of her I do estate unto Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: 而佢係我嘅,我對佢嘅一切權利,我都授予狄米特律斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而她是我的,我對她的一切權利,我都授予狄米特律斯。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: I am, my lord, as well deriv’d as he, As well possess’d;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅大人,我嘅出身同佢一樣好,財產都一樣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的大人,我的出身和他一樣好,財產也一樣;

passages.original: my love is more than his; My fortunes every way as fairly rank’d, If not with vantage, as Demetrius’;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅愛比佢嘅多;我嘅財運喺各方面都排得一樣好,如果唔係更占優勢,比狄米特律斯嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的愛比他的多;我的財運在各方面都排得一樣好,如果不是更占優勢,比狄米特律斯的;

passages.original: And, which is more than all these boasts can be, I am belov’d of beauteous Hermia.
passages.vernacular: 而比所有呢啲誇耀更重要嘅係,我被美麗嘅赫米婭所愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而比所有這些誇耀更重要的是,我被美麗的赫米婭所愛。

passages.original: Why should not I then prosecute my right?
passages.vernacular: 嗰我點解不追求我嘅權利?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我為什麼不追求我的權利?

passages.original: Demetrius, I’ll avouch it to his head, Made love to Nedar’s daughter, Helena, And won her soul;
passages.vernacular: 狄米特律斯,我要當面證實,佢向尼達嘅女兒海倫娜求過愛,贏得咗佢嘅靈魂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄米特律斯,我要當面證實,他向尼達的女兒海倫娜求過愛,贏得了她的靈魂;

passages.original: and she, sweet lady, dotes, Devoutly dotes, dotes in idolatry, Upon this spotted and inconstant man.
passages.vernacular: 而佢,甜美嘅小姐,癡癡地迷戀,虔誠地迷戀,偶像崇拜般地迷戀呢個有污點、反覆無常嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而她,甜美的小姐,癡癡地迷戀,虔誠地迷戀,偶像崇拜般地迷戀這個有污點、反覆無常的人。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: I must confess that I have heard so much, And with Demetrius thought to have spoke thereof;
passages.vernacular: 我必須承認我聽講過呢啲,本想同狄米特律斯談呢事;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須承認我聽說過這些,本想同狄米特律斯談這事;

passages.original: But, being over-full of self-affairs, My mind did lose it.—But, Demetrius, come, And come, Egeus; you shall go with me.
passages.vernacular: 但因為被自己嘅事務塞得太滿,我嘅心把呢事忘喇。——但係,狄米特律斯,嚟,伊吉斯,你都嚟;你哋跟我走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但因為被自己的事務塞得太滿,我的心把這事忘了。——但是,狄米特律斯,來,伊吉斯,你也來;你們跟我走。

passages.original: I have some private schooling for you both.— For you, fair Hermia, look you arm yourself To fit your fancies to your father’s will, Or else the law of Athens yields you up (Which by no means we may extenuate) To death, or to a vow of single life.
passages.vernacular: 我有些私下嘅教誨要畀你哋倆。——至於你,美麗嘅赫米婭,你要武裝好自己,使你嘅幻想順從你父親嘅意願,否則雅典嘅法律(我哋絕唔能夠減輕)會把你交畀死亡,或單身嘅誓願。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有些私下的教誨要給你們倆。——至於你,美麗的赫米婭,你要武裝好自己,使你的幻想順從你父親的意願,否則雅典的法律(我們絕不能減輕)會把你交給死亡,或單身的誓願。

passages.original: Come, my Hippolyta.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我嘅希波呂忒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我的希波呂忒。

passages.original: What cheer, my love?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,我嘅愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,我的愛?

passages.original: Demetrius and Egeus, go along; I must employ you in some business Against our nuptial, and confer with you Of something nearly that concerns yourselves.
passages.vernacular: 狄米特律斯同伊吉斯,跟我嚟;我必須為了我哋嘅婚禮派你哋辦些事,並同你哋商量啲同你哋切身相關嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄米特律斯和伊吉斯,跟我來;我必須為了我們的婚禮派你們辦些事,並同你們商量一些與你們切身相關的事。

passages.title: Egeus 伊吉斯
passages.original: With duty and desire we follow you.
passages.vernacular: 我哋懷住責任同願望跟隨您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們懷著責任與願望跟隨您。

passages.original: [Exeunt all but Lysander and Hermia.]
passages.vernacular: [除拉山德同赫米婭外眾人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [除拉山德和赫米婭外眾人下。]

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: How now, my love?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,我嘅愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,我的愛?

passages.original: Why is your cheek so pale?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅臉頰點解咁蒼白?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的臉頰為什麼這麼蒼白?

passages.original: How chance the roses there do fade so fast?
passages.vernacular: 嗰度嘅玫瑰點凋謝得咁快?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡的玫瑰怎麼凋謝得這麼快?

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Belike for want of rain, which I could well Beteem them from the tempest of my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 大概係缺雨,我可以用我眼睛嘅風暴好好畀佢哋澆灌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大概是缺雨,我可以用我眼睛的風暴好好給它們澆灌。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Ay me!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀!

passages.original: For aught that I could ever read, Could ever hear by tale or history, The course of true love never did run smooth.
passages.vernacular: 就我讀到嘅、聽故事或歷史所知嘅,真愛嘅路從來不平坦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就我讀到的、聽故事或歷史所知的,真愛的路從來不平坦。

passages.original: But either it was different in blood—
passages.vernacular: 要麼係血統不同——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼是血統不同——

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: O cross!
passages.vernacular: 啊,阻礙!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,阻礙!

passages.original: Too high to be enthrall’d to low.
passages.vernacular: 地位高嘅竟被低嘅奴役。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 地位高的竟被低的奴役。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Or else misgraffèd in respect of years—
passages.vernacular: 要麼嫁接得同年齡不相稱——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼嫁接得與年齡不相稱——

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: O spite!
passages.vernacular: 啊,惡意!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,惡意!

passages.original: Too old to be engag’d to young.
passages.vernacular: 老嘅竟許配畀少嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老的竟許配給少的。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Or else it stood upon the choice of friends—
passages.vernacular: 要麼取決於朋友嘅選擇——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼取決於朋友的選擇——

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: O hell!
passages.vernacular: 啊,地獄!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,地獄!

passages.original: to choose love by another’s eyes!
passages.vernacular: 要通過別人嘅眼睛選擇愛情!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要通過別人的眼睛選擇愛情!

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Or, if there were a sympathy in choice, War, death, or sickness did lay siege to it, Making it momentany as a sound, Swift as a shadow, short as any dream, Brief as the lightning in the collied night That, in a spleen, unfolds both heaven and earth, And, ere a man hath power to say, ‘Behold!’
passages.vernacular: 或者,即使選擇上有同感,戰爭、死亡或疾病圍攻佢,使佢轉瞬即逝如聲音,迅疾如影子,短暫如夢,簡短如黑漆漆嘅夜裡嘅閃電,喺一時之怒中展開天同地,喺人仲冇嚟得及講「睇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,即使選擇上有同感,戰爭、死亡或疾病圍攻它,使它轉瞬即逝如聲音,迅疾如影子,短暫如夢,簡短如黑漆漆的夜裡的閃電,在一時之怒中展開天與地,在人還沒來得及說「看!」

passages.original: The jaws of darkness do devour it up: So quick bright things come to confusion.
passages.vernacular: 黑暗嘅口就把佢吞食:光亮嘅事物就咁樣迅速歸於毀滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑暗的口就把它吞食:光亮的事物就這樣迅速歸於毀滅。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: If then true lovers have ever cross’d, It stands as an edict in destiny.
passages.vernacular: 如果真正嘅戀人總是受阻,嗰個就係命運中嘅一道法令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果真正的戀人總是受阻,那就是命運中的一道法令。

passages.original: Then let us teach our trial patience, Because it is a customary cross, As due to love as thoughts and dreams and sighs, Wishes and tears, poor fancy’s followers.
passages.vernacular: 咁讓我哋教導我哋嘅考驗要有耐心,因為呢個係慣常嘅磨難,對愛情來講係應得嘅,如同思想、夢、嘆息、願望同眼淚,可憐嘅幻想嘅隨從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼讓我們教導我們的考驗要有耐心,因為這是慣常的磨難,對愛情來說是應得的,如同思想、夢、嘆息、願望和眼淚,可憐的幻想的隨從。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: A good persuasion; therefore, hear me, Hermia.
passages.vernacular: 好講法;所以,聽我講,赫米婭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好說法;所以,聽我說,赫米婭。

passages.original: I have a widow aunt, a dowager Of great revenue, and she hath no child.
passages.vernacular: 我有一位寡婦姑母,係個好有收入嘅老夫人,佢冇細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一位寡婦姑母,是個很有收入的老夫人,她沒有孩子。

passages.original: From Athens is her house remote seven leagues, And she respects me as her only son.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅家離雅典七里格遠,佢把我當獨生子般睇重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的家離雅典七里格遠,她把我當獨生子般看重。

passages.original: There, gentle Hermia, may I marry thee, And to that place the sharp Athenian law Cannot pursue us.
passages.vernacular: 溫柔嘅赫米婭,喺嗰度我可以娶你,尖銳嘅雅典法律追唔到我哋嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫柔的赫米婭,在那裡我可以娶你,尖銳的雅典法律追不到我們那裡。

passages.original: If thou lovest me then, Steal forth thy father’s house tomorrow night;
passages.vernacular: 如果你愛我,就喺明晚偷偷溜出你父親嘅家;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你愛我,就在明晚偷偷溜出你父親的家;

passages.original: And in the wood, a league without the town (Where I did meet thee once with Helena To do observance to a morn of May), There will I stay for thee.
passages.vernacular: 喺城外一里格嘅樹林裡(我曾喺嗰度同海倫娜一起遇見你,慶祝五月嘅早晨),我會喺嗰度等你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在城外一里格的樹林裡(我曾在那裡同海倫娜一起遇見你,慶祝五月的早晨),我會在那裡等你。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: My good Lysander!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅好拉山德!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的好拉山德!

passages.original: I swear to thee by Cupid’s strongest bow, By his best arrow with the golden head, By the simplicity of Venus’ doves, By that which knitteth souls and prospers loves, And by that fire which burn’d the Carthage queen When the false Trojan under sail was seen, By all the vows that ever men have broke (In number more than ever women spoke), In that same place thou hast appointed me, Tomorrow truly will I meet with thee.
passages.vernacular: 我憑丘比特最強嘅弓,憑佢最好嘅金頭箭,憑維納斯鴿子嘅單純,憑嗰使靈魂相結並使愛情興旺嘅,憑嗰曾燒灼迦太基女王嘅火,當佢睇見虛假嘅特洛伊人揚帆而去,憑男人曾背棄嘅所有誓言(其數目比女人所講嘅任何時候都多),喺你指定嘅嗰個地方,聽日我一定同你會面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我憑丘比特最強的弓,憑他最好的金頭箭,憑維納斯鴿子的單純,憑那使靈魂相結並使愛情興旺的,憑那曾燒灼迦太基女王的火,當她看見虛假的特洛伊人揚帆而去,憑男人曾背棄的所有誓言(其數目比女人所說的任何時候都多),在你指定的那個地方,明天我一定同你會面。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Keep promise, love.
passages.vernacular: 守約,愛人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 守約,愛人。

passages.original: Look, here comes Helena.
passages.vernacular: 睇,海倫娜嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,海倫娜來了。

passages.original: Enter Helena.
passages.vernacular: [海倫娜上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [海倫娜上。]

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: God speed fair Helena!
passages.vernacular: 願上帝保佑美麗嘅海倫娜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝保佑美麗的海倫娜!

passages.original: Whither away?
passages.vernacular: 你往邊度去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你往哪裡去?

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: Call you me fair?
passages.vernacular: 你叫我美麗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫我美麗?

passages.original: That fair again unsay.
passages.vernacular: 請收回嗰個「美麗」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請收回那個「美麗」。

passages.original: Demetrius loves your fair.
passages.vernacular: 狄米特律斯愛你嘅美麗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄米特律斯愛你的美麗。

passages.original: O happy fair!
passages.vernacular: 啊幸福嘅美麗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊幸福的美麗!

passages.original: Your eyes are lode-stars and your tongue’s sweet air More tuneable than lark to shepherd’s ear, When wheat is green, when hawthorn buds appear.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅眼睛係北極星,你嘅舌頭嘅甜美曲調,比麥子青綠、山楂花蕾出現時牧羊人耳中嘅雲雀更悅耳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的眼睛是北極星,你的舌頭的甜美曲調,比麥子青綠、山楂花蕾出現時牧羊人耳中的雲雀更悅耳。

passages.original: Sickness is catching.
passages.vernacular: 疾病會傳染。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 疾病會傳染。

passages.original: O were favour so, Yours would I catch, fair Hermia, ere I go.
passages.vernacular: 啊,但願美貌都咁樣,美麗嘅赫米婭,我離開前就會染上你嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,但願美貌也這樣,美麗的赫米婭,我離開前就會染上你的:

passages.original: My ear should catch your voice, my eye your eye, My tongue should catch your tongue’s sweet melody.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅耳朵會染上你嘅聲音,我嘅眼睛染上你嘅眼睛,我嘅舌頭染上你舌頭嘅甜美旋律。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的耳朵會染上你的聲音,我的眼睛染上你的眼睛,我的舌頭染上你舌頭的甜美旋律。

passages.original: Were the world mine, Demetrius being bated, The rest I’d give to be to you translated.
passages.vernacular: 若全世界係我嘅,除咗狄米特律斯,其餘我都願意送出,只為變成你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 若全世界是我的,除了狄米特律斯,其餘我都願意送出,只為變成你。

passages.original: O, teach me how you look, and with what art You sway the motion of Demetrius’ heart!
passages.vernacular: 啊,教我你嘅神情,同你用乜嘢手段左右狄米特律斯嘅心!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,教我你的神情,和你用什麼手段左右狄米特律斯的心!

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: I frown upon him, yet he loves me still.
passages.vernacular: 我對佢皺眉,佢卻仍愛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對他皺眉,他卻仍愛我。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: O that your frowns would teach my smiles such skill!
passages.vernacular: 啊但願你嘅皺眉能教我嘅微笑咁樣嘅本領!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊但願你的皺眉能教我的微笑這樣的本領!

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: I give him curses, yet he gives me love.
passages.vernacular: 我咒罵佢,佢卻畀我愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我咒罵他,他卻給我愛。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: O that my prayers could such affection move!
passages.vernacular: 啊但願我嘅祈禱能引起咁樣嘅感情!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊但願我的祈禱能引起這樣的感情!

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: The more I hate, the more he follows me.
passages.vernacular: 我越恨,佢越追我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我越恨,他越追我。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: The more I love, the more he hateth me.
passages.vernacular: 我越愛,佢越恨我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我越愛,他越恨我。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: His folly, Helena, is no fault of mine.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅愚蠢,海倫娜,唔係我嘅錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的愚蠢,海倫娜,不是我的錯。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: None but your beauty; would that fault were mine!
passages.vernacular: 除咗你嘅美貌,冇別嘅;但願嗰過錯係我嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了你的美貌,沒有別的;但願那過錯是我的!

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Take comfort: he no more shall see my face; Lysander and myself will fly this place.
passages.vernacular: 放心:佢再都見唔到我嘅臉;拉山德同我將逃離呢個地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放心:他再也見不到我的臉;拉山德和我將逃離這個地方。

passages.original: Before the time I did Lysander see, Seem’d Athens as a paradise to me.
passages.vernacular: 喺我見到拉山德之前,雅典對我像天堂一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我見到拉山德之前,雅典對我像天堂一樣。

passages.original: O, then, what graces in my love do dwell, That he hath turn’d a heaven into hell!
passages.vernacular: 啊,咁我嘅愛人身上有乜嘢魅力,竟把天堂變成地獄!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那麼我的愛人身上有什麼魅力,竟把天堂變成地獄!

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Helen, to you our minds we will unfold: Tomorrow night, when Phoebe doth behold Her silver visage in the watery glass, Decking with liquid pearl the bladed grass (A time that lovers’ flights doth still conceal), Through Athens’ gates have we devis’d to steal.
passages.vernacular: 海倫,我哋要向你透露我哋嘅心意:明晚,當月神菲碧喺水鏡中睇見自己嘅銀色臉龐,用液態珍珠點綴葉片般嘅草(呢個時辰總是能掩護戀人出逃),我哋已計劃偷偷穿過雅典城門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海倫,我們要向你透露我們的心意:明晚,當月神菲碧在水鏡中看見自己的銀色臉龐,用液態珍珠點綴葉片般的草(這個時辰總是能掩護戀人出逃),我們已計劃偷偷穿過雅典城門。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: And in the wood where often you and I Upon faint primrose beds were wont to lie, Emptying our bosoms of their counsel sweet, There my Lysander and myself shall meet, And thence from Athens turn away our eyes, To seek new friends and stranger companies.
passages.vernacular: 喺樹林裡,你我常喺淡淡嘅報春花床上躺臥,傾倒心中甜蜜嘅秘密,我嘅拉山德同我就喺嗰度會面,然後從雅典轉開我哋嘅眼睛,去尋找新朋友同陌生嘅同伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在樹林裡,你我常在淡淡的報春花床上躺臥,傾倒心中甜蜜的秘密,我的拉山德和我就在那裡會面,然後從雅典轉開我們的眼睛,去尋找新朋友和陌生的同伴。

passages.original: Farewell, sweet playfellow.
passages.vernacular: 再會,甜美嘅玩伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,甜美的玩伴。

passages.original: Pray thou for us, And good luck grant thee thy Demetrius!
passages.vernacular: 為我哋祈禱,願好運把你嘅狄米特律斯賜畀你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為我們祈禱,願好運把你的狄米特律斯賜給你!

passages.original: Keep word, Lysander.
passages.vernacular: 守約,拉山德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 守約,拉山德。

passages.original: We must starve our sight From lovers’ food, till morrow deep midnight.
passages.vernacular: 我哋必須讓我哋嘅眼睛挨餓,不食戀人嘅食糧,直到明晚深夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們必須讓我們的眼睛挨餓,不吃戀人的食糧,直到明晚深夜。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: I will, my Hermia.
passages.vernacular: 我會嘅,我嘅赫米婭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會的,我的赫米婭。

passages.original: [Exit Hermia.]
passages.vernacular: [赫米婭下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [赫米婭下。]

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Helena, adieu.
passages.vernacular: 海倫娜,再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海倫娜,再會。

passages.original: As you on him, Demetrius dote on you!
passages.vernacular: 願狄米特律斯迷戀你,如同你迷戀佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願狄米特律斯迷戀你,如同你迷戀他!

passages.original: [Exit Lysander.]
passages.vernacular: [拉山德下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拉山德下。]

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: How happy some o’er other some can be!
passages.vernacular: 有些人比另啲人快樂多少!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人比另一些人快樂多少!

passages.original: Through Athens I am thought as fair as she.
passages.vernacular: 全雅典都認為我同佢一樣美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全雅典都認為我和她一樣美。

passages.original: But what of that?
passages.vernacular: 但嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那又怎樣?

passages.original: Demetrius thinks not so; He will not know what all but he do know.
passages.vernacular: 狄米特律斯不咁樣想;佢唔肯知道所有人都知道嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄米特律斯不這樣想;他不肯知道所有人都知道的事。

passages.original: And as he errs, doting on Hermia’s eyes, So I, admiring of his qualities.
passages.vernacular: 就像佢迷戀赫米婭嘅眼睛而錯喇,我都因欣賞佢嘅品質而錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像他迷戀赫米婭的眼睛而錯了,我也因欣賞他的品質而錯了。

passages.original: Things base and vile, holding no quantity, Love can transpose to form and dignity.
passages.vernacular: 卑賤醜陋、毫無分量嘅嘢,愛情能把佢變成形狀同尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卑賤醜陋、毫無分量的東西,愛情能把它變成形狀和尊嚴。

passages.original: Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind;
passages.vernacular: 愛情唔使眼睛睇,而用心睇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛情不用眼睛看,而用心看;

passages.original: And therefore is wing’d Cupid painted blind.
passages.vernacular: 所以長翅膀嘅丘比特被畫成瞎子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以長翅膀的丘比特被畫成瞎子。

passages.original: Nor hath love’s mind of any judgment taste.
passages.vernacular: 愛情嘅心都毫無判斷嘅品味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛情的心也毫無判斷的品味。

passages.original: Wings, and no eyes, figure unheedy haste.
passages.vernacular: 有翅膀,冇眼睛,象徵不加思索嘅匆忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有翅膀,沒眼睛,象徵不加思索的匆忙。

passages.original: And therefore is love said to be a child, Because in choice he is so oft beguil’d.
passages.vernacular: 所以愛情被講成係個細路,因為佢喺選擇上咁常常受騙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以愛情被說成是個孩子,因為他在選擇上這麼常常受騙。

passages.original: As waggish boys in game themselves forswear, So the boy Love is perjur’d everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 就像淘氣嘅男孩喺遊戲中違背自己嘅誓言,男孩愛神都到處背誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像淘氣的男孩在遊戲中違背自己的誓言,男孩愛神也到處背誓。

passages.original: For, ere Demetrius look’d on Hermia’s eyne, He hail’d down oaths that he was only mine;
passages.vernacular: 因為,喺狄米特律斯睇到赫米婭嘅眼睛之前,佢曾像冰雹般發誓講佢只屬於我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為,在狄米特律斯看到赫米婭的眼睛之前,他曾像冰雹般發誓說他只屬於我;

passages.original: And when this hail some heat from Hermia felt, So he dissolv’d, and showers of oaths did melt.
passages.vernacular: 而當呢冰雹感受到赫米婭嘅啲熱度,佢就融化喇,誓言嘅陣雨都消融喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而當這冰雹感受到赫米婭的一些熱度,他就融化了,誓言的陣雨也消融了。

passages.original: I will go tell him of fair Hermia’s flight.
passages.vernacular: 我要去告訴佢美麗赫米婭出逃嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要去告訴他美麗赫米婭出逃的事。

passages.original: Then to the wood will he tomorrow night Pursue her;
passages.vernacular: 咁明晚佢會追佢到樹林去;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼明晚他會追她到樹林去;

passages.original: and for this intelligence If I have thanks, it is a dear expense.
passages.vernacular: 為呢個消息,如果我得到感謝,嗰個係昂貴嘅代價。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為這個消息,如果我得到感謝,那是昂貴的代價。

passages.original: But herein mean I to enrich my pain, To have his sight thither and back again.
passages.vernacular: 但我打算借此豐富我嘅痛苦,讓佢能去嗰度再回嚟地睇見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我打算借此豐富我的痛苦,讓他能去那裡再回來地看見他。

passages.original: [Exit Helena.]
passages.vernacular: [海倫娜下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [海倫娜下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene II — A Room in a Cottage 第一幕第二場:一間村屋

passages.original: Enter Quince, Snug, Bottom, Flute, Snout and Starveling.
passages.vernacular: [昆斯、斯納格、波頓、弗魯特、斯諾特同斯塔夫林上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [昆斯、斯納格、波頓、弗魯特、斯諾特與斯塔夫林上。]

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Is all our company here?
passages.vernacular: 我哋整個劇團都到齊咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們整個劇團都到齊了嗎?

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: You were best to call them generally, man by man, according to the scrip.
passages.vernacular: 你最好按名單逐個點名。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最好按名單逐個點名。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Here is the scroll of every man’s name, which is thought fit through all Athens, to play in our interlude before the Duke and Duchess, on his wedding-day at night.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係每個人嘅名字嘅卷軸,全雅典都認為適合喺公爵同公爵夫人婚禮當晚,喺佢哋面前演我哋嘅插劇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是每個人的名字的卷軸,全雅典都認為適合在公爵和公爵夫人婚禮當晚,在他們面前演我們的插劇。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: First, good Peter Quince, say what the play treats on;
passages.vernacular: 首先,好彼得·昆斯,講講呢齣戲講乜嘢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先,好彼得·昆斯,說說這齣戲講什麼;

passages.original: then read the names of the actors; and so grow to a point.
passages.vernacular: 然後念演員嘅名字;咁樣就切入要點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後念演員的名字;這樣就切入要點。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Marry, our play is The most lamentable comedy and most cruel death of Pyramus and Thisbe.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我哋嘅戲係《皮拉姆斯同提斯柏最悲慘嘅喜劇同最殘酷嘅死亡》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我們的戲是《皮拉姆斯和提斯柏最悲慘的喜劇和最殘酷的死亡》。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: A very good piece of work, I assure you, and a merry.
passages.vernacular: 我向你保證,係好好嘅作品,而且好笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向你保證,是很好的作品,而且好笑。

passages.original: Now, good Peter Quince, call forth your actors by the scroll.
passages.vernacular: 而家,好彼得·昆斯,照卷軸叫你嘅演員出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,好彼得·昆斯,照卷軸叫你的演員出來。

passages.original: Masters, spread yourselves.
passages.vernacular: 各位,散開站好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各位,散開站好。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Answer, as I call you.
passages.vernacular: 我叫到邊個就答應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫到誰就答應。

passages.original: Nick Bottom, the weaver.
passages.vernacular: 尼克·波頓,織工。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尼克·波頓,織工。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Ready.
passages.vernacular: 喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在。

passages.original: Name what part I am for, and proceed.
passages.vernacular: 講出我演乜嘢角色,然後繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說出我演什麼角色,然後繼續。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: You, Nick Bottom, are set down for Pyramus.
passages.vernacular: 你,尼克·波頓,被定為皮拉姆斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,尼克·波頓,被定為皮拉姆斯。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: What is Pyramus—a lover, or a tyrant?
passages.vernacular: 皮拉姆斯係乜嘢——情人,定係暴君?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮拉姆斯是什麼——情人,還是暴君?

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: A lover, that kills himself most gallantly for love.
passages.vernacular: 一個情人,為愛情最英勇地自殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個情人,為愛情最英勇地自殺。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: That will ask some tears in the true performing of it.
passages.vernacular: 要把佢真正演好,得要些眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要把它真正演好,得要些眼淚。

passages.original: If I do it, let the audience look to their eyes.
passages.vernacular: 如果我嚟演,就讓觀眾當心佢哋嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我來演,就讓觀眾當心他們的眼睛。

passages.original: I will move storms; I will condole in some measure.
passages.vernacular: 我要掀起風暴;我要喺某種程度上哀悼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要掀起風暴;我要在某種程度上哀悼。

passages.original: To the rest—yet my chief humour is for a tyrant.
passages.vernacular: 對其他人——不過我主要嘅脾氣係演暴君。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對其他人——不過我主要的脾氣是演暴君。

passages.original: I could play Ercles rarely, or a part to tear a cat in, to make all split.
passages.vernacular: 我可以把赫拉克勒斯演得出色,或者演一個撕貓嘅角色,使一切裂開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以把赫拉克勒斯演得出色,或者演一個撕貓的角色,使一切裂開。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: The raging rocks And shivering shocks Shall break the locks Of prison gates, And Phibbus’ car Shall shine from far, And make and mar The foolish Fates.
passages.vernacular: 狂暴嘅岩石同顫抖嘅衝擊將打破監獄大門嘅鎖,太陽神嘅車從遠方閃耀,製造並毀掉愚蠢嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狂暴的岩石和顫抖的衝擊將打破監獄大門的鎖,太陽神的車從遠方閃耀,製造並毀掉愚蠢的命運。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: This was lofty.
passages.vernacular: 呢個好崇高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這很崇高。

passages.original: Now name the rest of the players.
passages.vernacular: 而家講其餘演員嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在說其餘演員的名字。

passages.original: This is Ercles’ vein, a tyrant’s vein; a lover is more condoling.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係赫拉克勒斯嘅風格,暴君嘅風格;情人更悲慟些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是赫拉克勒斯的風格,暴君的風格;情人更悲慟些。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Francis Flute, the bellows-mender.
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西斯·弗魯特,修風箱嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西斯·弗魯特,修風箱的。

passages.title: Flute 弗魯特
passages.original: Here, Peter Quince.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,彼得·昆斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,彼得·昆斯。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Flute, you must take Thisbe on you.
passages.vernacular: 弗魯特,你必須扮演提斯柏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗魯特,你必須扮演提斯柏。

passages.title: Flute 弗魯特
passages.original: What is Thisbe?
passages.vernacular: 提斯柏係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提斯柏是什麼?

passages.original: A wandering knight?
passages.vernacular: 一位流浪騎士嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位流浪騎士嗎?

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: It is the lady that Pyramus must love.
passages.vernacular: 係皮拉姆斯必須愛上嘅嗰位小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是皮拉姆斯必須愛上的那位小姐。

passages.title: Flute 弗魯特
passages.original: Nay, faith, let not me play a woman.
passages.vernacular: 不,講真嘅,唔好畀我演女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,說真的,別讓我演女人。

passages.original: I have a beard coming.
passages.vernacular: 我鬍子快長出嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我鬍子快長出來了。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: That’s all one.
passages.vernacular: 冇關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒關係。

passages.original: You shall play it in a mask, and you may speak as small as you will.
passages.vernacular: 你戴面具演,你可以盡量尖住嗓子講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你戴面具演,你可以盡量尖著嗓子說話。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: And I may hide my face, let me play Thisbe too.
passages.vernacular: 如果我能遮住臉,就讓我都演提斯柏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我能遮住臉,就讓我也演提斯柏。

passages.original: I’ll speak in a monstrous little voice; ‘Thisne, Thisne!’—‘Ah, Pyramus, my lover dear!
passages.vernacular: 我要用可怕嘅小聲音講:「提斯內,提斯內!」——「啊,皮拉姆斯,我親愛嘅愛人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要用可怕的小聲音說:「提斯內,提斯內!」——「啊,皮拉姆斯,我親愛的愛人!

passages.original: thy Thisbe dear!
passages.vernacular: 你親愛嘅提斯柏!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你親愛的提斯柏!

passages.original: and lady dear!’
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅小姐!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的小姐!」

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: No, no, you must play Pyramus; and, Flute, you Thisbe.
passages.vernacular: 不,不,你必須演皮拉姆斯;弗魯特,你演提斯柏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不,你必須演皮拉姆斯;弗魯特,你演提斯柏。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Well, proceed.
passages.vernacular: 好,繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,繼續。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Robin Starveling, the tailor.
passages.vernacular: 羅賓·斯塔夫林,裁縫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅賓·斯塔夫林,裁縫。

passages.title: Starveling 斯塔夫林
passages.original: Here, Peter Quince.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,彼得·昆斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,彼得·昆斯。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Robin Starveling, you must play Thisbe’s mother.
passages.vernacular: 羅賓·斯塔夫林,你必須演提斯柏嘅母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅賓·斯塔夫林,你必須演提斯柏的母親。

passages.original: Tom Snout, the tinker.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆·斯諾特,補鍋匠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆·斯諾特,補鍋匠。

passages.title: Snout 斯諾特
passages.original: Here, Peter Quince.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,彼得·昆斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,彼得·昆斯。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: You, Pyramus’ father; myself, Thisbe’s father;
passages.vernacular: 你,皮拉姆斯嘅父親;我自己,提斯柏嘅父親;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,皮拉姆斯的父親;我自己,提斯柏的父親;

passages.original: Snug, the joiner, you, the lion’s part.
passages.vernacular: 斯納格,細木工,你,獅子嘅角色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯納格,細木工,你,獅子的角色。

passages.original: And, I hope here is a play fitted.
passages.vernacular: 我希望呢齣戲配齊喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望這齣戲配齊了。

passages.title: Snug 斯納格
passages.original: Have you the lion’s part written?
passages.vernacular: 你寫好獅子嘅台詞咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你寫好獅子的台詞了嗎?

passages.original: Pray you, if it be, give it me, for I am slow of study.
passages.vernacular: 請你,如果寫好喇,畀我,因為我背書慢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,如果寫好了,給我,因為我背書慢。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: You may do it extempore, for it is nothing but roaring.
passages.vernacular: 你可以即興演,因為只係吼叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以即興演,因為只是吼叫。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Let me play the lion too.
passages.vernacular: 讓我都演獅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我也演獅子。

passages.original: I will roar that I will do any man’s heart good to hear me.
passages.vernacular: 我要吼得讓所有人聽咗心裡舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要吼得讓所有人聽了心裡舒服。

passages.original: I will roar that I will make the Duke say ‘Let him roar again, let him roar again.’
passages.vernacular: 我要吼得讓公爵講「讓佢再吼一次,讓佢再吼一次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要吼得讓公爵說「讓他再吼一次,讓他再吼一次。」

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: If you should do it too terribly, you would fright the Duchess and the ladies, that they would shriek;
passages.vernacular: 如果你吼得太嚇人,你會嚇到公爵夫人同女士哋,使佢哋尖叫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你吼得太嚇人,你會嚇到公爵夫人和女士們,使她們尖叫;

passages.original: and that were enough to hang us all.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就足以把我哋全都吊死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就足以把我們全都吊死。

passages.title: All 眾人
passages.original: That would hang us every mother’s son.
passages.vernacular: 嗰會把我哋每個母親嘅兒子都吊死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會把我們每個母親的兒子都吊死。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: I grant you, friends, if you should fright the ladies out of their wits, they would have no more discretion but to hang us.
passages.vernacular: 我同意,朋友哋,如果你嚇得女士哋失魂落魄,佢哋就冇別嘅判斷,只會把我哋吊死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我同意,朋友們,如果你嚇得女士們失魂落魄,她們就沒有別的判斷,只會把我們吊死。

passages.original: But I will aggravate my voice so, that I will roar you as gently as any sucking dove;
passages.vernacular: 但我要把我嘅聲音加重,吼得像食奶嘅鴿子一樣溫和;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我要把我的聲音加重,吼得像吃奶的鴿子一樣溫和;

passages.original: I will roar you an ’twere any nightingale.
passages.vernacular: 我要吼得像夜鶯一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要吼得像夜鶯一樣。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: You can play no part but Pyramus, for Pyramus is a sweet-faced man;
passages.vernacular: 你只能演皮拉姆斯,因為皮拉姆斯係個面容俊美嘅人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只能演皮拉姆斯,因為皮拉姆斯是個面容俊美的人;

passages.original: a proper man as one shall see in a summer’s day;
passages.vernacular: 係人哋喺夏天一天裡能見到嘅最體面嘅男人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是人們在夏天一天裡能見到的最體面的男人;

passages.original: a most lovely gentleman-like man.
passages.vernacular: 一位最可愛嘅紳士風度嘅男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位最可愛的紳士風度的男人。

passages.original: Therefore you must needs play Pyramus.
passages.vernacular: 所以你必須演皮拉姆斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你必須演皮拉姆斯。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Well, I will undertake it.
passages.vernacular: 好,我嚟承擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我來承擔。

passages.original: What beard were I best to play it in?
passages.vernacular: 我戴乜嘢鬍子演最好?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我戴什麼鬍子演最好?

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Why, what you will.
passages.vernacular: 哎,隨你鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,隨你喜歡。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: I will discharge it in either your straw-colour beard, your orange-tawny beard, your purple-in-grain beard, or your French-crown-colour beard, your perfect yellow.
passages.vernacular: 我可以戴你嗰稻草色鬍子,你嗰橙黃褐色鬍子,你嗰深紫色鬍子,或你嗰法國金幣色鬍子,你嗰純黃色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以戴你那稻草色鬍子,你那橙黃褐色鬍子,你那深紫色鬍子,或你那法國金幣色鬍子,你那純黃色。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Some of your French crowns have no hair at all, and then you will play bare-faced.
passages.vernacular: 你嗰啲法國金幣色嘅有些根本冇毛,嗰你就得光住臉演。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你那些法國金幣色的有些根本沒毛,那你就得光著臉演。

passages.original: But, masters, here are your parts, and I am to entreat you, request you, and desire you, to con them by tomorrow night;
passages.vernacular: 但係,各位,呢個係你哋嘅角色,我要懇求你哋,請求你哋,希望你哋,明晚前背熟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,各位,這是你們的角色,我要懇求你們,請求你們,希望你們,明晚前背熟;

passages.original: and meet me in the palace wood, a mile without the town, by moonlight;
passages.vernacular: 並喺月光下到宮殿樹林見我,離城一英里;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並在月光下到宮殿樹林見我,離城一英里;

passages.original: there will we rehearse, for if we meet in the city, we shall be dogg’d with company, and our devices known.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺嗰度排練,因為如果我哋喺城裡見面,會被人跟蹤,我哋嘅計劃就被知道喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在那裡排練,因為如果我們在城裡見面,會被人跟蹤,我們的計劃就被知道了。

passages.original: In the meantime I will draw a bill of properties, such as our play wants.
passages.vernacular: 同時我會開一張道具清單,我哋嘅戲需要嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時我會開一張道具清單,我們的戲需要的那種。

passages.original: I pray you fail me not.
passages.vernacular: 請你哋唔好讓我失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你們不要讓我失望。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: We will meet, and there we may rehearse most obscenely and courageously.
passages.vernacular: 我哋會見面,喺嗰度我哋可以排練得最下流、最勇敢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會見面,在那裡我們可以排練得最下流、最勇敢。

passages.original: Take pains, be perfect; adieu.
passages.vernacular: 努力,背熟;再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 努力,背熟;再會。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: At the Duke’s oak we meet.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺公爵嘅橡樹下見面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在公爵的橡樹下見面。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Enough.
passages.vernacular: 夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夠了。

passages.original: Hold, or cut bow-strings.
passages.vernacular: 守住,否則割斷弓弦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 守住,否則割斷弓弦。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene I — A Wood near Athens 第二幕第一場:雅典附近的樹林

passages.original: Enter a Fairy at one door, and Puck at another.
passages.vernacular: [一位仙子從一道門,帕克從另一道門上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一位仙子從一道門,帕克從另一道門上。]

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: How now, spirit!
passages.vernacular: 點喇,精靈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,精靈!

passages.original: Whither wander you?
passages.vernacular: 你往邊度漫遊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你往哪裡漫遊?

passages.title: Fairy 小仙子
passages.original: Over hill, over dale, Thorough bush, thorough brier, Over park, over pale, Thorough flood, thorough fire, I do wander everywhere, Swifter than the moon’s sphere;
passages.vernacular: 越過山,越過谷,穿過灌木,穿過荊棘,越過園囿,越過籬笆,穿過洪水,穿過烈火,我到處漫遊,比月亮嘅軌道仲快;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 越過山,越過谷,穿過灌木,穿過荊棘,越過園囿,越過籬笆,穿過洪水,穿過烈火,我到處漫遊,比月亮的軌道還快;

passages.original: And I serve the Fairy Queen, To dew her orbs upon the green.
passages.vernacular: 我服侍仙后,喺草地上為佢嘅圓圈灑露水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我服侍仙后,在草地上為她的圓圈灑露水。

passages.original: The cowslips tall her pensioners be, In their gold coats spots you see;
passages.vernacular: 高高嘅黃花九輪草係佢嘅衛士,你睇佢哋金外套上嘅斑點;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高高的黃花九輪草是她的衛士,你看他們金外套上的斑點;

passages.original: Those be rubies, fairy favours, In those freckles live their savours.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係紅寶石,仙子嘅恩賜,喺嗰啲雀斑裡住佢哋嘅香氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是紅寶石,仙子的恩賜,在那些雀斑裡住著她們的香氣。

passages.original: I must go seek some dew-drops here, And hang a pearl in every cowslip’s ear.
passages.vernacular: 我得去呢度找些露珠,喺每朵黃花九輪草嘅耳朵上掛一顆珍珠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得去這裡找些露珠,在每朵黃花九輪草的耳朵上掛一顆珍珠。

passages.original: Farewell, thou lob of spirits; I’ll be gone.
passages.vernacular: 再會,你呢笨拙嘅精靈;我走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,你這笨拙的精靈;我走了。

passages.original: Our Queen and all her elves come here anon.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅皇后同佢所有嘅小精靈即刻就到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的皇后和她所有的小精靈馬上就到這裡。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: The King doth keep his revels here tonight; Take heed the Queen come not within his sight, For Oberon is passing fell and wrath, Because that she, as her attendant, hath A lovely boy, stol’n from an Indian king;
passages.vernacular: 國王今晚喺呢度開宴會;留意唔好畀王后出而家佢視線內,因為奧布朗正極為凶狠憤怒,因為佢有一個可愛嘅男孩當侍從,係從一位印度國王嗰度偷嚟嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王今晚在這裡開宴會;留意別讓王后出現在他視線內,因為奧布朗正極為凶狠憤怒,因為她有一個可愛的男孩當侍從,是從一位印度國王那裡偷來的;

passages.original: She never had so sweet a changeling.
passages.vernacular: 佢從冇過咁樣可愛嘅換嚟嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從沒有過這樣可愛的換來的孩子。

passages.original: And jealous Oberon would have the child Knight of his train, to trace the forests wild:
passages.vernacular: 而妒忌嘅奧布朗想要呢個細路做佢隨從嘅騎士,喺野林中追蹤:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而妒忌的奧布朗想要這個孩子做他隨從的騎士,在野林中追蹤:

passages.original: But she perforce withholds the lovèd boy, Crowns him with flowers, and makes him all her joy.
passages.vernacular: 但佢硬係唔肯放手呢個被愛嘅男孩,畀佢戴花冠,使佢成為佢全部嘅歡喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她硬是不肯放手這個被愛的男孩,給他戴花冠,使他成為她全部的歡喜。

passages.original: And now they never meet in grove or green, By fountain clear, or spangled starlight sheen, But they do square;
passages.vernacular: 而家佢哋喺樹叢或草地,喺清泉邊或星光閃爍嘅夜色中相遇,都要吵架;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他們在樹叢或草地,在清泉邊或星光閃爍的夜色中相遇,都要吵架;

passages.original: that all their elves for fear Creep into acorn cups, and hide them there.
passages.vernacular: 嚇得佢哋所有嘅小精靈都爬進橡果杯裡躲起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嚇得他們所有的小精靈都爬進橡果杯裡躲起來。

passages.title: Fairy 小仙子
passages.original: Either I mistake your shape and making quite, Or else you are that shrewd and knavish sprite Call’d Robin Goodfellow.
passages.vernacular: 要麼我完全認錯咗你嘅外形同長相,要麼你就係嗰個機靈搗蛋嘅精靈,叫羅賓·好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼我完全認錯了你的外形和長相,要麼你就是那個機靈搗蛋的精靈,叫羅賓·好朋友。

passages.original: Are not you he That frights the maidens of the villagery, Skim milk, and sometimes labour in the quern, And bootless make the breathless housewife churn, And sometime make the drink to bear no barm, Mislead night-wanderers, laughing at their harm?
passages.vernacular: 你不就係嗰個嚇唬村裡少女、撇去牛奶上嘅奶皮、有時喺磨坊裡幹活、使氣喘吁吁嘅主婦白費力氣地攪奶油、有時使飲料不起泡、讓夜行者迷路、並嘲笑佢哋嘅不幸嘅人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不就是那個嚇唬村裡少女、撇去牛奶上的奶皮、有時在磨坊裡幹活、使氣喘吁吁的主婦白費力氣地攪奶油、有時使飲料不起泡、讓夜行者迷路、並嘲笑他們的不幸的人嗎?

passages.original: Those that Hobgoblin call you, and sweet Puck, You do their work, and they shall have good luck.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲稱呼你為妖精、親切嘅帕克嘅人,你替佢哋幹活,佢哋就會有好運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些稱呼你為妖精、親切的帕克的人,你替他們幹活,他們就會有好運。

passages.original: Are not you he?
passages.vernacular: 你不就係佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不就是他嗎?

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Thou speak’st aright; I am that merry wanderer of the night.
passages.vernacular: 你講得對;我就係嗰個快樂嘅夜遊者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說得對;我就是那個快樂的夜遊者。

passages.original: I jest to Oberon, and make him smile, When I a fat and bean-fed horse beguile, Neighing in likeness of a filly foal;
passages.vernacular: 我對奧布朗開玩笑,逗佢笑,當我欺騙一匹食豆子嘅肥馬,學住小母馬嘶鳴;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對奧布朗開玩笑,逗他笑,當我欺騙一匹吃豆子的肥馬,學著小母馬嘶鳴;

passages.original: And sometime lurk I in a gossip’s bowl In very likeness of a roasted crab, And, when she drinks, against her lips I bob, And on her withered dewlap pour the ale.
passages.vernacular: 有時我潛伏喺長舌婦嘅碗裡,睇起嚟就像一個烤熟嘅野蘋果,當佢飲酒時,我就撞佢嘅嘴唇,把啤酒灑喺佢乾癟嘅下垂喉肉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我潛伏在長舌婦的碗裡,看起來就像一個烤熟的野蘋果,當她喝酒時,我就撞她的嘴唇,把啤酒灑在她乾癟的下垂喉肉上。

passages.original: The wisest aunt, telling the saddest tale, Sometime for three-foot stool mistaketh me;
passages.vernacular: 最聰明嘅姑媽,講住最悲傷嘅故事,有時把我錯當成三腳凳;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最聰明的姑媽,說著最悲傷的故事,有時把我錯當成三腳凳;

passages.original: Then slip I from her bum, down topples she, And ‘tailor’ cries, and falls into a cough;
passages.vernacular: 然後我從佢屁股下溜開,佢就翻倒,喊「裁縫!」,跌得咳嗽起嚟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我從她屁股下溜開,她就翻倒,喊「裁縫!」,跌得咳嗽起來;

passages.original: And then the whole quire hold their hips and loffe And waxen in their mirth, and neeze, and swear A merrier hour was never wasted there.
passages.vernacular: 然後整個合唱團捧住髖骨大笑,越笑越樂,打噴嚏,發誓講嗰度從冇浪費過更快樂嘅一小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後整個合唱團捧著髖骨大笑,越笑越樂,打噴嚏,發誓說那裡從沒浪費過更快樂的一小時。

passages.original: But room, fairy.
passages.vernacular: 但讓路,仙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但讓路,仙子。

passages.original: Here comes Oberon.
passages.vernacular: 奧布朗嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧布朗來了。

passages.title: Fairy 小仙子
passages.original: And here my mistress.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人在這裡。

passages.original: Would that he were gone!
passages.vernacular: 但願佢走開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願他走開!

passages.original: Enter Oberon at one door, with his Train, and Titania at another, with hers.
passages.vernacular: [奧布朗偕隨從從一道門,蒂塔妮婭偕佢嘅隨從從另一道門上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧布朗偕隨從從一道門,蒂塔妮婭偕她的隨從從另一道門上。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Ill met by moonlight, proud Titania.
passages.vernacular: 月光下不幸相遇,驕傲嘅蒂塔妮婭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月光下不幸相遇,驕傲的蒂塔妮婭。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: What, jealous Oberon!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,妒忌嘅奧布朗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,妒忌的奧布朗!

passages.original: Fairies, skip hence; I have forsworn his bed and company.
passages.vernacular: 仙子哋,從呢度蹦開;我已發誓唔再同佢同床同伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙子們,從這裡蹦開;我已發誓不再同他同床同伴。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Tarry, rash wanton; am not I thy lord?
passages.vernacular: 等一等,輕率嘅任性鬼;我唔係你嘅主人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等一等,輕率的任性鬼;我不是你的主人嗎?

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Then I must be thy lady; but I know When thou hast stol’n away from fairyland, And in the shape of Corin sat all day Playing on pipes of corn, and versing love To amorous Phillida.
passages.vernacular: 嗰我就必須係你嘅夫人;但我知道你乜嘢時候偷偷離開仙境,化身成科林,整天坐住吹麥桿笛,對多情嘅菲麗達念情詩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我就必須是你的夫人;但我知道你什麼時候偷偷離開仙境,化身成科林,整天坐著吹麥桿笛,對多情的菲麗達念情詩。

passages.original: Why art thou here, Come from the farthest steep of India, But that, forsooth, the bouncing Amazon, Your buskin’d mistress and your warrior love, To Theseus must be wedded;
passages.vernacular: 你點解喺呢度,從印度最遠嘅山崖嚟,不就係因為,真嘅,嗰位活蹦亂跳嘅亞馬遜女戰士,你穿厚底靴嘅情婦同戰士情人,要嫁畀忒修斯;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼在這裡,從印度最遠的山崖來,不就是因為,真的,那位活蹦亂跳的亞馬遜女戰士,你穿厚底靴的情婦和戰士情人,要嫁給忒修斯;

passages.original: and you come To give their bed joy and prosperity?
passages.vernacular: 而你嚟係要畀佢哋嘅婚床賜福同興旺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而你來是要給他們的婚床賜福和興旺?

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: How canst thou thus, for shame, Titania, Glance at my credit with Hippolyta, Knowing I know thy love to Theseus?
passages.vernacular: 蒂塔妮婭,你點咁樣唔知羞恥,暗指我同希波呂忒嘅名聲,明明知道我知道你對忒修斯嘅愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂塔妮婭,你怎麼這樣不知羞恥,暗指我與希波呂忒的名聲,明明知道我知道你對忒修斯的愛?

passages.original: Didst not thou lead him through the glimmering night From Perigenia, whom he ravished?
passages.vernacular: 你唔係喺閃爍嘅夜裡領佢離開珀里吉尼亞,佢曾強暴佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是在閃爍的夜裡領他離開珀里吉尼亞,他曾強暴她嗎?

passages.original: And make him with fair Aegles break his faith, With Ariadne and Antiopa?
passages.vernacular: 並讓佢同美麗嘅埃格勒、阿里阿德涅同安提俄珀背棄誓言?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並讓他同美麗的埃格勒、阿里阿德涅和安提俄珀背棄誓言?

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: These are the forgeries of jealousy: And never, since the middle summer’s spring, Met we on hill, in dale, forest, or mead, By pavèd fountain, or by rushy brook, Or on the beachèd margent of the sea, To dance our ringlets to the whistling wind, But with thy brawls thou hast disturb’d our sport.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲都係妒忌嘅捏造:自從仲夏之春以來,我哋喺山上、谷中、森林或草地、鋪石嘅泉邊、蘆葦嘅溪旁、或鋪滿鵝卵石嘅海岸,想隨住呼嘯嘅風跳我哋嘅圓環舞時,你總是用吵鬧打斷我哋嘅遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些都是妒忌的捏造:自從仲夏之春以來,我們在山上、谷中、森林或草地、鋪石的泉邊、蘆葦的溪旁、或鋪滿鵝卵石的海岸,想隨著呼嘯的風跳我們的圓環舞時,你總是用吵鬧打斷我們的遊戲。

passages.original: Therefore the winds, piping to us in vain, As in revenge, have suck’d up from the sea Contagious fogs;
passages.vernacular: 所以風對我哋吹奏卻徒然,彷彿為了報復,從海上吸起有傳染性嘅霧;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以風對我們吹奏卻徒然,彷彿為了報復,從海上吸起有傳染性的霧;

passages.original: which, falling in the land, Hath every pelting river made so proud That they have overborne their continents.
passages.vernacular: 霧落喺地上,使每條微不足道嘅小河變得咁驕傲,以致漫過咗堤岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 霧落在地上,使每條微不足道的小河變得這麼驕傲,以致漫過了堤岸。

passages.original: The ox hath therefore stretch’d his yoke in vain, The ploughman lost his sweat, and the green corn Hath rotted ere his youth attain’d a beard.
passages.vernacular: 所以牛徒勞地拉住軛,農夫白費咗汗水,青綠嘅麥子喺長出鬍鬚之前就腐爛喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以牛徒勞地拉著軛,農夫白費了汗水,青綠的麥子在長出鬍鬚之前就腐爛了。

passages.original: The fold stands empty in the drownèd field, And crows are fatted with the murrion flock;
passages.vernacular: 羊圈喺淹沒嘅田野中空住,烏鴉因瘟死嘅羊群而肥胖;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羊圈在淹沒的田野中空著,烏鴉因瘟死的羊群而肥胖;

passages.original: The nine-men’s-morris is fill’d up with mud, And the quaint mazes in the wanton green, For lack of tread, are undistinguishable.
passages.vernacular: 九人莫里斯棋盤被泥填滿,而放縱嘅草地上精巧嘅迷宮,因無人踩踏而無法分辨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 九人莫里斯棋盤被泥填滿,而放縱的草地上精巧的迷宮,因無人踩踏而無法分辨。

passages.original: The human mortals want their winter here.
passages.vernacular: 凡人喺呢度缺少佢哋嘅冬天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡人在這裡缺少他們的冬天。

passages.original: No night is now with hymn or carol blest.
passages.vernacular: 而家冇一夜被讚美詩或頌歌所祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在沒有一夜被讚美詩或頌歌所祝福。

passages.original: Therefore the moon, the governess of floods, Pale in her anger, washes all the air, That rheumatic diseases do abound.
passages.vernacular: 所以月亮,潮汐嘅主宰,因憤怒而蒼白,洗遍整個空氣,使風濕病大量流行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以月亮,潮汐的主宰,因憤怒而蒼白,洗遍整個空氣,使風濕病大量流行。

passages.original: And thorough this distemperature we see The seasons alter:
passages.vernacular: 由於呢氣候失調,我哋睇到季節改變:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 由於這氣候失調,我們看到季節改變:

passages.original: hoary-headed frosts Fall in the fresh lap of the crimson rose;
passages.vernacular: 白頭嘅霜落喺鮮紅玫瑰嘅新鮮懷裡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白頭的霜落在鮮紅玫瑰的新鮮懷裡;

passages.original: And on old Hiems’ thin and icy crown An odorous chaplet of sweet summer buds Is, as in mockery, set.
passages.vernacular: 喺老冬神希姆斯薄薄嘅冰冠上,一頂芬芳嘅夏日花蕾花環,彷彿嘲弄似地被戴上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在老冬神希姆斯薄薄的冰冠上,一頂芬芳的夏日花蕾花環,彷彿嘲弄似地被戴上。

passages.original: The spring, the summer, The childing autumn, angry winter, change Their wonted liveries;
passages.vernacular: 春天、夏天、多產嘅秋天、憤怒嘅冬天,更換咗佢哋慣常嘅服裝;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 春天、夏天、多產的秋天、憤怒的冬天,更換了它們慣常的服裝;

passages.original: and the mazed world, By their increase, now knows not which is which.
passages.vernacular: 而困惑嘅世界,由於佢哋嘅增多,而家分不清邊個係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而困惑的世界,由於它們的增多,現在分不清誰是誰。

passages.original: And this same progeny of evils comes From our debate, from our dissension;
passages.vernacular: 而呢一整批禍害來自我哋嘅爭吵、我哋嘅不同;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而這一整批禍害來自我們的爭吵、我們的不和;

passages.original: We are their parents and original.
passages.vernacular: 我哋係佢哋嘅父母同源頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們是它們的父母和源頭。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Do you amend it, then.
passages.vernacular: 咁你去改正佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼你去改正它。

passages.original: It lies in you.
passages.vernacular: 呢取決於你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這取決於你。

passages.original: Why should Titania cross her Oberon?
passages.vernacular: 蒂塔妮婭點解要違逆佢嘅奧布朗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂塔妮婭為什麼要違逆她的奧布朗?

passages.original: I do but beg a little changeling boy To be my henchman.
passages.vernacular: 我不過係求一個換嚟嘅小男孩做我嘅侍從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不過是求一個換來的小男孩做我的侍從。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Set your heart at rest; The fairyland buys not the child of me.
passages.vernacular: 放心吧;整個仙境都唔能夠從我手裡買走呢細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放心吧;整個仙境也不能從我手裡買走這孩子。

passages.original: His mother was a vot’ress of my order, And in the spicèd Indian air, by night, Full often hath she gossip’d by my side;
passages.vernacular: 佢母親係我修會嘅一位信徒,喺香料瀰漫嘅印度空氣裡,夜裡常常喺我身邊閒聊;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他母親是我修會的一位信徒,在香料瀰漫的印度空氣裡,夜裡常常在我身邊閒聊;

passages.original: And sat with me on Neptune’s yellow sands, Marking th’ embarkèd traders on the flood, When we have laugh’d to see the sails conceive, And grow big-bellied with the wanton wind;
passages.vernacular: 佢同我坐喺海神黃色嘅沙灘上,睇住水上滿載嘅商船,我哋笑睇風帆懷孕,被放縱嘅風吹成大肚子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她同我坐在海神黃色的沙灘上,看著水上滿載的商船,我們笑看風帆懷孕,被放縱的風吹成大肚子;

passages.original: Which she, with pretty and with swimming gait Following (her womb then rich with my young squire), Would imitate, and sail upon the land, To fetch me trifles, and return again, As from a voyage, rich with merchandise.
passages.vernacular: 佢用優美、輕飄嘅步態模仿住(佢當時嘅子宮因我年輕嘅侍從而豐盈),喺陸地上航行,去畀我取小玩意,然後回嚟,像從航行歸嚟,滿載貨物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用優美、輕飄的步態模仿著(她當時的子宮因我年輕的侍從而豐盈),在陸地上航行,去給我取小玩意,然後回來,像從航行歸來,滿載貨物。

passages.original: But she, being mortal, of that boy did die; And for her sake do I rear up her boy, And for her sake I will not part with him.
passages.vernacular: 但佢係凡人,為嗰細路而死;為了佢嘅緣故,我撫養佢嘅細路,為了佢嘅緣故,我不放走佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她是凡人,為那孩子而死;為了她的緣故,我撫養她的孩子,為了她的緣故,我不放走他。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: How long within this wood intend you stay?
passages.vernacular: 你打算喺呢樹林裡待多久?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你打算在這樹林裡待多久?

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Perchance till after Theseus’ wedding-day.
passages.vernacular: 或者到忒修斯嘅婚禮之後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許到忒修斯的婚禮之後。

passages.original: If you will patiently dance in our round, And see our moonlight revels, go with us;
passages.vernacular: 如果你肯耐心地加入我哋嘅圓舞,睇我哋月光下嘅狂歡,就跟我哋嚟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你肯耐心地加入我們的圓舞,看我們月光下的狂歡,就跟我們來;

passages.original: If not, shun me, and I will spare your haunts.
passages.vernacular: 如果不,就躲開我,我會放過你嘅出冇之地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不,就躲開我,我會放過你的出沒之地。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Give me that boy and I will go with thee.
passages.vernacular: 把嗰細路畀我,我就跟你走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把那孩子給我,我就跟你走。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Not for thy fairy kingdom.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅整個仙國畀我都不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的整個仙國給我也不行。

passages.original: Fairies, away.
passages.vernacular: 仙子哋,走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙子們,走。

passages.original: We shall chide downright if I longer stay.
passages.vernacular: 我若再待下去,我哋就要大吵喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我若再待下去,我們就要大吵了。

passages.original: [Exit Titania with her Train.]
passages.vernacular: [蒂塔妮婭偕隨從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [蒂塔妮婭偕隨從下。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Well, go thy way.
passages.vernacular: 好,走你嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,走你的路。

passages.original: Thou shalt not from this grove Till I torment thee for this injury.— My gentle Puck, come hither.
passages.vernacular: 你不離開呢片樹林,我就要為呢傷害折磨你。——我溫和嘅帕克,嚟呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不離開這片樹林,我就要為這傷害折磨你。——我溫和的帕克,來這裡。

passages.original: Thou rememb’rest Since once I sat upon a promontory, And heard a mermaid on a dolphin’s back Uttering such dulcet and harmonious breath That the rude sea grew civil at her song And certain stars shot madly from their spheres To hear the sea-maid’s music.
passages.vernacular: 你記得嗎,有一次我坐喺海岬上,聽見一個人魚騎喺海豚背上,吐出咁甜美和諧嘅氣息,連粗野嘅海都被佢嘅歌聲馴服,有些星星為聽海中少女嘅音樂,從軌道瘋狂地射落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你記得嗎,有一次我坐在海岬上,聽見一個人魚騎在海豚背上,吐出那麼甜美和諧的氣息,連粗野的海也被她的歌聲馴服,有些星星為聽海中少女的音樂,從軌道瘋狂地射落。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: I remember.
passages.vernacular: 我記得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: That very time I saw, (but thou couldst not), Flying between the cold moon and the earth, Cupid all arm’d:
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰時我睇見(但你睇唔見),喺冷月同大地之間飛行,全副武裝嘅丘比特:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那時我看見(但你看不見),在冷月與大地之間飛行,全副武裝的丘比特:

passages.original: a certain aim he took At a fair vestal, thronèd by the west, And loos’d his love-shaft smartly from his bow As it should pierce a hundred thousand hearts.
passages.vernacular: 佢瞄準咗一位美麗嘅女祭司,佢坐喺西方嘅寶座上,佢靈巧地從弓上射出佢嘅愛情之箭,好像要刺穿十萬顆心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他瞄準了一位美麗的女祭司,她坐在西方的寶座上,他靈巧地從弓上射出他的愛情之箭,好像要刺穿十萬顆心。

passages.original: But I might see young Cupid’s fiery shaft Quench’d in the chaste beams of the watery moon;
passages.vernacular: 但我睇見年輕丘比特嘅火箭,喺水汪汪月亮嘅貞潔光線中熄滅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我看見年輕丘比特的火箭,在水汪汪月亮的貞潔光線中熄滅;

passages.original: And the imperial votress passed on, In maiden meditation, fancy-free.
passages.vernacular: 嗰帝王般嘅女祭司繼續前行,喺處女嘅沉思中,心無牽掛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那帝王般的女祭司繼續前行,在處女的沉思中,心無牽掛。

passages.original: Yet mark’d I where the bolt of Cupid fell: It fell upon a little western flower, Before milk-white, now purple with love’s wound, And maidens call it love-in-idleness.
passages.vernacular: 然而我注意到丘比特嘅箭落喺邊度:佢落喺一朵西方嘅小花上,原本乳白,而家因愛嘅傷口而紫紅,少女哋稱佢「懶散嘅愛」(三色堇)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而我注意到丘比特的箭落在哪裡:它落在一朵西方的小花上,原本乳白,現在因愛的傷口而紫紅,少女們稱它「懶散的愛」(三色堇)。

passages.original: Fetch me that flower, the herb I showed thee once:
passages.vernacular: 畀我取嗰朵花,我曾指畀你睇嘅嗰種草:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我取那朵花,我曾指給你看的那種草:

passages.original: The juice of it on sleeping eyelids laid Will make or man or woman madly dote Upon the next live creature that it sees.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅汁液塗喺沉瞓嘅眼瞼上,會使男人或女人瘋狂地迷戀醒嚟睇見嘅下一個活物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的汁液塗在沉睡的眼瞼上,會使男人或女人瘋狂地迷戀醒來看見的下一個活物。

passages.original: Fetch me this herb, and be thou here again Ere the leviathan can swim a league.
passages.vernacular: 畀我取呢種草,喺巨鯨游一里格之前回到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我取這種草,在巨鯨游一里格之前回到這裡。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: I’ll put a girdle round about the earth In forty minutes.
passages.vernacular: 我可以喺四好鐘內為大地繞上一圈腰帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以在四十分鐘內為大地繞上一圈腰帶。

passages.original: [Exit Puck.]
passages.vernacular: [帕克下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [帕克下。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Having once this juice, I’ll watch Titania when she is asleep, And drop the liquor of it in her eyes:
passages.vernacular: 一旦得到呢汁液,我就要喺蒂塔妮婭瞓住時睇住佢,把佢嘅液體滴喺佢眼裡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一旦得到這汁液,我就要在蒂塔妮婭睡著時看著她,把它的液體滴在她眼裡:

passages.original: The next thing then she waking looks upon (Be it on lion, bear, or wolf, or bull, On meddling monkey, or on busy ape) She shall pursue it with the soul of love.
passages.vernacular: 佢醒嚟睇見嘅下一樣嘢(無論係獅子、熊、狼或公牛,係多事嘅猴子,或忙碌嘅猿),佢都會以愛嘅靈魂追求佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她醒來看見的下一樣東西(無論是獅子、熊、狼或公牛,是多事的猴子,或忙碌的猿),她都會以愛的靈魂追求它。

passages.original: And ere I take this charm from off her sight (As I can take it with another herb) I’ll make her render up her page to me.
passages.vernacular: 喺我把呢魔法從佢眼中解除之前(我可以用另一種草解除),我要讓佢把佢嘅侍童交畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我把這魔法從她眼中解除之前(我可以用另一種草解除),我要讓她把她的侍童交給我。

passages.original: But who comes here?
passages.vernacular: 但邊個嚟喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但誰來了?

passages.original: I am invisible; And I will overhear their conference.
passages.vernacular: 我係隱形嘅;我要偷聽佢哋嘅談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是隱形的;我要偷聽他們的談話。

passages.original: Enter Demetrius, Helena following him.
passages.vernacular: [狄米特律斯上,海倫娜跟隨佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [狄米特律斯上,海倫娜跟隨他。]

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: I love thee not, therefore pursue me not.
passages.vernacular: 我不愛你,所以別追我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不愛你,所以別追我。

passages.original: Where is Lysander and fair Hermia?
passages.vernacular: 拉山德同美麗嘅赫米婭喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉山德和美麗的赫米婭在哪裡?

passages.original: The one I’ll slay, the other slayeth me.
passages.vernacular: 一個我要殺,另一個喺殺我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個我要殺,另一個在殺我。

passages.original: Thou told’st me they were stol’n into this wood, And here am I, and wode within this wood Because I cannot meet with Hermia.
passages.vernacular: 你告訴我佢哋溜進咗呢片樹林,而我喺呢度,喺呢樹林裡發瘋,因為遇唔到赫米婭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你告訴我他們溜進了這片樹林,而我在這裡,在這樹林裡發瘋,因為遇不到赫米婭。

passages.original: Hence, get thee gone, and follow me no more.
passages.vernacular: 走開,滾,唔好再跟住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開,滾,別再跟著我。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: You draw me, you hard-hearted adamant, But yet you draw not iron, for my heart Is true as steel.
passages.vernacular: 你吸引我,你呢鐵石心腸嘅金剛石,不過你吸不動鐵,因為我嘅心像鋼一樣忠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你吸引我,你這鐵石心腸的金剛石,可是你吸不動鐵,因為我的心像鋼一樣忠實。

passages.original: Leave you your power to draw, And I shall have no power to follow you.
passages.vernacular: 你放棄你吸引嘅力量,我就冇力量追隨你喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你放棄你吸引的力量,我就沒有力量追隨你了。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Do I entice you?
passages.vernacular: 我引誘你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我引誘你嗎?

passages.original: Do I speak you fair?
passages.vernacular: 我對你講好話嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對你說好話嗎?

passages.original: Or rather do I not in plainest truth Tell you I do not, nor I cannot love you?
passages.vernacular: 定係我唔係最明白地告訴你我不愛你,都唔能夠愛你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是我不是最明白地告訴你我不愛你,也不能愛你?

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: And even for that do I love you the more.
passages.vernacular: 而正是為此,我更愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而正是為此,我更愛你。

passages.original: I am your spaniel; and, Demetrius, The more you beat me, I will fawn on you.
passages.vernacular: 我係你嘅獵犬;狄米特律斯,你越打我,我越向你搖尾巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是你的獵犬;狄米特律斯,你越打我,我越向你搖尾巴。

passages.original: Use me but as your spaniel, spurn me, strike me, Neglect me, lose me;
passages.vernacular: 只把我當作你嘅獵犬對待,踢我,打我,不理我,丟掉我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只把我當作你的獵犬對待,踢我,打我,不理我,丟掉我;

passages.original: only give me leave, Unworthy as I am, to follow you.
passages.vernacular: 只求准許我,雖然我不配,跟住你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只求准許我,雖然我不配,跟著你。

passages.original: What worser place can I beg in your love, (And yet a place of high respect with me) Than to be usèd as you use your dog?
passages.vernacular: 喺你嘅愛情裡,我仲能求乜嘢比呢更壞嘅位置(然而喺我心中嗰個係極受重視嘅位置),比被你像對待你嘅狗一樣對待?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在你的愛情裡,我還能求什麼比這更壞的位置(然而在我心中那是極受重視的位置),比被你像對待你的狗一樣對待?

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Tempt not too much the hatred of my spirit; For I am sick when I do look on thee.
passages.vernacular: 別太過試探我精神中嘅恨;因為我一睇你就覺得噁心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別太過試探我精神中的恨;因為我一看你就覺得噁心。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: And I am sick when I look not on you.
passages.vernacular: 而我不睇你就覺得噁心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我不看你就覺得噁心。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: You do impeach your modesty too much To leave the city and commit yourself Into the hands of one that loves you not, To trust the opportunity of night And the ill counsel of a desert place, With the rich worth of your virginity.
passages.vernacular: 你太過損害你嘅端莊喇,離開城市,把自己交到一個不愛你嘅人手裡,把夜晚嘅機會同荒野地方嘅壞勸告,信賴於你貴重嘅貞潔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你太過損害你的端莊了,離開城市,把自己交到一個不愛你的人手裡,把夜晚的機會和荒野地方的壞勸告,信賴於你貴重的貞潔。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: Your virtue is my privilege: for that It is not night when I do see your face, Therefore I think I am not in the night;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅美德係我嘅特權:因為我睇見你嘅臉時就唔係夜晚,所以我想我不喺夜裡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的美德是我的特權:因為我看見你的臉時就不是夜晚,所以我想我不在夜裡;

passages.original: Nor doth this wood lack worlds of company, For you, in my respect, are all the world.
passages.vernacular: 呢樹林都不缺乏千萬同伴,因為你對我來講就係全世界。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樹林也不缺乏千萬同伴,因為你對我來說就是全世界。

passages.original: Then how can it be said I am alone When all the world is here to look on me?
passages.vernacular: 咁點能講我係獨自一人,既然全世界都喺呢度睇住我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼怎麼能說我是獨自一人,既然全世界都在這裡看著我?

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: I’ll run from thee and hide me in the brakes, And leave thee to the mercy of wild beasts.
passages.vernacular: 我要從你呢度跑開,藏進灌木叢,把你留畀野獸嘅憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要從你這裡跑開,藏進灌木叢,把你留給野獸的憐憫。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: The wildest hath not such a heart as you.
passages.vernacular: 最野嘅野獸都冇你咁樣嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最野的野獸也沒有你這樣的心。

passages.original: Run when you will, the story shall be chang’d;
passages.vernacular: 隨你跑,故事要改喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨你跑,故事要改了;

passages.original: Apollo flies, and Daphne holds the chase; The dove pursues the griffin, the mild hind Makes speed to catch the tiger.
passages.vernacular: 阿波羅逃跑,達芙妮追趕;鴿子追趕獅鷲,溫順嘅母鹿急追老虎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿波羅逃跑,達芙妮追趕;鴿子追趕獅鷲,溫順的母鹿急追老虎。

passages.original: Bootless speed, When cowardice pursues and valour flies!
passages.vernacular: 徒勞嘅疾行,當懦弱追趕、勇敢逃跑!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 徒勞的疾行,當懦弱追趕、勇敢逃跑!

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: I will not stay thy questions.
passages.vernacular: 我不留下聽你嘅追問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不留下聽你的追問。

passages.original: Let me go, Or if thou follow me, do not believe But I shall do thee mischief in the wood.
passages.vernacular: 讓我走,或者如果你跟我,別不相信我會喺樹林裡傷害你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我走,或者如果你跟我,別不相信我會在樹林裡傷害你。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: Ay, in the temple, in the town, the field, You do me mischief.
passages.vernacular: 對,喺神殿裡、喺城裡、喺田野裡,你都喺傷害我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,在神殿裡、在城裡、在田野裡,你都在傷害我。

passages.original: Fie, Demetrius!
passages.vernacular: 呸,狄米特律斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,狄米特律斯!

passages.original: Your wrongs do set a scandal on my sex.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅惡行畀我嘅性別蒙上咗醜聞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的惡行給我的性別蒙上了醜聞。

passages.original: We cannot fight for love as men may do.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔能夠像男人嗰樣為愛而戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不能像男人那樣為愛而戰。

passages.original: We should be woo’d, and were not made to woo.
passages.vernacular: 我哋應被追求,而唔係生來追求嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們應被追求,而不是生來追求的。

passages.original: [Exit Demetrius.]
passages.vernacular: [狄米特律斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [狄米特律斯下。]

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: I’ll follow thee, and make a heaven of hell, To die upon the hand I love so well.
passages.vernacular: 我要跟住你,把地獄變成天堂,死喺我如此深愛嘅手上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要跟著你,把地獄變成天堂,死在我如此深愛的手上。

passages.original: [Exit Helena.]
passages.vernacular: [海倫娜下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [海倫娜下。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Fare thee well, nymph.
passages.vernacular: 再會,仙女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,仙女。

passages.original: Ere he do leave this grove, Thou shalt fly him, and he shall seek thy love.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢離開呢片樹林之前,你將逃避佢,佢將尋求你嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他離開這片樹林之前,你將逃避他,他將尋求你的愛。

passages.original: Enter Puck.
passages.vernacular: [帕克上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [帕克上。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Hast thou the flower there?
passages.vernacular: 你有嗰朵花嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有那朵花嗎?

passages.original: Welcome, wanderer.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,漫遊者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,漫遊者。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Ay, there it is.
passages.vernacular: 有,喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,在這裡。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: I pray thee give it me.
passages.vernacular: 請你畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你給我。

passages.original: I know a bank where the wild thyme blows, Where oxlips and the nodding violet grows, Quite over-canopied with luscious woodbine, With sweet musk-roses, and with eglantine.
passages.vernacular: 我知道一處河岸,野百里香開放,黃花九輪草同點頭嘅紫羅蘭生長,上面完全由甜美嘅忍冬、甜麝香玫瑰同野薔薇遮蓋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道一處河岸,野百里香開放,黃花九輪草和點頭的紫羅蘭生長,上面完全由甜美的忍冬、甜麝香玫瑰和野薔薇遮蓋。

passages.original: There sleeps Titania sometime of the night, Lull’d in these flowers with dances and delight;
passages.vernacular: 蒂塔妮婭有時夜裡瞓喺嗰度,喺呢啲花中被舞蹈同歡樂哄瞓;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂塔妮婭有時夜裡睡在那裡,在這些花中被舞蹈和歡樂哄睡;

passages.original: And there the snake throws her enamell’d skin, Weed wide enough to wrap a fairy in.
passages.vernacular: 蛇喺嗰度蛻下佢琺瑯般嘅皮,嗰衣裳寬得足以裹住一個仙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蛇在那裡蛻下她琺瑯般的皮,那衣裳寬得足以裹住一個仙子。

passages.original: And with the juice of this I’ll streak her eyes, And make her full of hateful fantasies.
passages.vernacular: 我要用呢花嘅汁液抹佢嘅眼睛,讓佢充滿可憎嘅幻覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要用這花的汁液抹她的眼睛,讓她充滿可憎的幻覺。

passages.original: Take thou some of it, and seek through this grove:
passages.vernacular: 你都攞啲,穿過呢片樹林去找:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也拿一些,穿過這片樹林去找:

passages.original: A sweet Athenian lady is in love With a disdainful youth.
passages.vernacular: 一位美麗嘅雅典小姐愛上咗一個不屑一顧嘅青年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位美麗的雅典小姐愛上了一個不屑一顧的青年。

passages.original: Anoint his eyes; But do it when the next thing he espies May be the lady.
passages.vernacular: 畀佢嘅眼睛抹上;但要喺佢醒嚟見到嘅下一樣嘢可能係嗰位小姐時才做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給他的眼睛抹上;但要在他醒來見到的下一樣東西可能是那位小姐時才做。

passages.original: Thou shalt know the man By the Athenian garments he hath on.
passages.vernacular: 你能從佢穿嘅雅典服裝認出嗰個男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能從他穿的雅典服裝認出那個男人。

passages.original: Effect it with some care, that he may prove More fond on her than she upon her love:
passages.vernacular: 小心辦妥,使佢對佢比佢對自己嘅愛更癡迷:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小心辦妥,使他對她比她對自己的愛更癡迷:

passages.original: And look thou meet me ere the first cock crow.
passages.vernacular: 並喺第一聲雞啼之前嚟見我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並在第一聲雞啼之前來見我。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Fear not, my lord, your servant shall do so.
passages.vernacular: 別怕,大人,您嘅僕人會咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別怕,大人,您的僕人會這樣做。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene II — Another Part of the Wood 第二幕第二場:樹林另一處

passages.original: Enter Titania with her Train.
passages.vernacular: [蒂塔妮婭偕隨從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [蒂塔妮婭偕隨從上。]

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Come, now a roundel and a fairy song; Then for the third part of a minute, hence;
passages.vernacular: 嚟,而家跳個圓舞,唱支仙子嘅歌;然後三分之一分鐘後,離開;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,現在跳個圓舞,唱支仙子的歌;然後三分之一分鐘後,離開;

passages.original: Some to kill cankers in the musk-rose buds; Some war with reremice for their leathern wings, To make my small elves coats;
passages.vernacular: 有些去殺死麝香玫瑰花蕾裡嘅蛀蟲;有些同蝙蝠作戰,取牠哋嘅皮翅,畀我嘅小精靈做外衣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些去殺死麝香玫瑰花蕾裡的蛀蟲;有些與蝙蝠作戰,取牠們的皮翅,給我的小精靈做外衣;

passages.original: and some keep back The clamorous owl, that nightly hoots and wonders At our quaint spirits.
passages.vernacular: 有些擋住嗰吵鬧嘅貓頭鷹,牠夜夜鳴叫,驚訝於我哋奇妙嘅精靈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些擋住那吵鬧的貓頭鷹,牠夜夜鳴叫,驚訝於我們奇妙的精靈。

passages.original: Sing me now asleep; Then to your offices, and let me rest.
passages.vernacular: 而家唱我入瞓;然後去做你哋嘅差事,讓我休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在唱我入睡;然後去做你們的差事,讓我休息。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Fairies sing.
passages.vernacular: 仙子哋唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙子們唱。

passages.title: First Fairy 第一小仙子
passages.original: You spotted snakes with double tongue, Thorny hedgehogs, be not seen;
passages.vernacular: 你哋帶斑點、有雙舌嘅蛇,多刺嘅刺蝟,唔好被睇見;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們帶斑點、有雙舌的蛇,多刺的刺蝟,不要被看見;

passages.original: Newts and blind-worms do no wrong, Come not near our Fairy Queen:
passages.vernacular: 蠑螈同盲蛇唔好作害,唔好靠近我哋嘅仙后:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蠑螈和盲蛇不要作害,不要靠近我們的仙后:

passages.title: Chorus 眾仙子
passages.original: Philomel, with melody, Sing in our sweet lullaby:
passages.vernacular: 夜鶯,用旋律,唱進我哋甜美嘅搖籃曲:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜鶯,用旋律,唱進我們甜美的搖籃曲:

passages.original: Lulla, lulla, lullaby; lulla, lulla, lullaby.
passages.vernacular: 啦,啦,搖籃曲;啦,啦,搖籃曲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啦,啦,搖籃曲;啦,啦,搖籃曲。

passages.original: Never harm, nor spell, nor charm, Come our lovely lady nigh;
passages.vernacular: 唔好傷害,唔好咒語,唔好魔法,靠近我哋可愛嘅夫人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要傷害,不要咒語,不要魔法,靠近我們可愛的夫人;

passages.original: So good night, with lullaby.
passages.vernacular: 所以晚安,伴住搖籃曲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以晚安,伴著搖籃曲。

passages.title: First Fairy 第一小仙子
passages.original: Weaving spiders, come not here; Hence, you long-legg’d spinners, hence.
passages.vernacular: 織網嘅蜘蛛,別嚟呢度;走開,你哋長腿嘅紡織工,走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 織網的蜘蛛,別來這裡;走開,你們長腿的紡織工,走開。

passages.original: Beetles black, approach not near; Worm nor snail do no offence.
passages.vernacular: 黑甲蟲,別靠近;蟲同蝸牛別冒犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑甲蟲,別靠近;蟲和蝸牛別冒犯。

passages.title: Chorus 眾仙子
passages.original: Philomel with melody, &c.
passages.vernacular: 夜鶯用旋律,等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜鶯用旋律,等等。

passages.title: Second Fairy 第二小仙子
passages.original: Hence away!
passages.vernacular: 走開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開!

passages.original: Now all is well.
passages.vernacular: 而家一切都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在一切都好。

passages.original: One aloof stand sentinel.
passages.vernacular: 一個站遠處放哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個站遠處放哨。

passages.original: [Exeunt Fairies. Titania sleeps.]
passages.vernacular: [仙子哋下。蒂塔妮婭入瞓。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [仙子們下。蒂塔妮婭入睡。]

passages.original: Enter Oberon.
passages.vernacular: [奧布朗上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧布朗上。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: What thou seest when thou dost wake,
passages.vernacular: 你醒嚟睇到嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你醒來看到的,

passages.original: [Squeezes the flower on Titania’s eyelids.]
passages.vernacular: [把花汁擠喺蒂塔妮婭嘅眼瞼上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [把花汁擠在蒂塔妮婭的眼瞼上。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Do it for thy true love take; Love and languish for his sake.
passages.vernacular: 都當作你真愛;為佢戀愛憔悴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都當作你真愛;為他戀愛憔悴。

passages.original: Be it ounce, or cat, or bear, Pard, or boar with bristled hair, In thy eye that shall appear When thou wak’st, it is thy dear.
passages.vernacular: 不論係山貓、貓、熊、豹,或係鬃毛豎起嘅野豬,你醒嚟時出而家你眼裡嘅,就係你嘅親愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不論是山貓、貓、熊、豹,或是鬃毛豎起的野豬,你醒來時出現在你眼裡的,就是你的親愛。

passages.original: Wake when some vile thing is near.
passages.vernacular: 喺有可憎嘅嘢靠近時醒嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在有可憎的東西靠近時醒來。

passages.original: [Exit.]
Enter Lysander and Hermia.
passages.vernacular: [拉山德同赫米婭上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拉山德與赫米婭上。]

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Fair love, you faint with wand’ring in the wood.
passages.vernacular: 美麗嘅愛人,你喺樹林裡漫遊累得發昏喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗的愛人,你在樹林裡漫遊累得發昏了。

passages.original: And, to speak troth, I have forgot our way.
passages.vernacular: 講實話,我都忘咗我哋嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說實話,我也忘了我們的路。

passages.original: We’ll rest us, Hermia, if you think it good, And tarry for the comfort of the day.
passages.vernacular: 我哋休息吧,赫米婭,如果你覺得好,並等待白天嘅安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們休息吧,赫米婭,如果你覺得好,並等待白天的安慰。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Be it so, Lysander: find you out a bed, For I upon this bank will rest my head.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣,拉山德:你去找張床,我就喺呢河岸上枕頭休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣,拉山德:你去找張床,我就在這河岸上枕頭休息。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: One turf shall serve as pillow for us both; One heart, one bed, two bosoms, and one troth.
passages.vernacular: 一塊草皮可作我哋兩人嘅枕頭;一顆心,一張床,兩個胸膛,一份誓約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一塊草皮可作我們兩人的枕頭;一顆心,一張床,兩個胸膛,一份誓約。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Nay, good Lysander; for my sake, my dear, Lie further off yet, do not lie so near.
passages.vernacular: 不,好拉山德;為了我,親愛嘅,躺遠啲,別躺咁近。
