passages.vernacular: 我從冇被詛咒過;我完全冇潑辣嘅天賦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒被詛咒過;我完全沒有潑辣的天賦;

passages.original: I am a right maid for my cowardice; Let her not strike me.
passages.vernacular: 我因膽小係個地道嘅少女;唔好畀佢打我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我因膽小是個地道的少女;別讓她打我。

passages.original: You perhaps may think, Because she is something lower than myself, That I can match her.
passages.vernacular: 你哋或者以為,因為佢比我矮啲,我就能對付佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們也許以為,因為她比我矮一點,我就能對付她。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Lower!
passages.vernacular: 矮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 矮!

passages.original: Hark, again.
passages.vernacular: 聽,又嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽,又來了。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: Good Hermia, do not be so bitter with me.
passages.vernacular: 好赫米婭,唔好對我咁樣苦澀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好赫米婭,不要對我這樣苦澀。

passages.original: I evermore did love you, Hermia, Did ever keep your counsels, never wrong’d you, Save that, in love unto Demetrius, I told him of your stealth unto this wood.
passages.vernacular: 我一向愛你,赫米婭,一向守你嘅秘密,從冇冤枉過你,只除咗出於對狄米特律斯嘅愛,我告訴佢你偷偷嚟呢樹林嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一向愛你,赫米婭,一向守你的秘密,從沒冤枉過你,只除了出於對狄米特律斯的愛,我告訴他你偷偷來這樹林的事。

passages.original: He follow’d you; for love I follow’d him; But he hath chid me hence, and threaten’d me To strike me, spurn me, nay, to kill me too:
passages.vernacular: 佢跟住你;出於愛我跟住佢;但佢把我趕走,威脅要打我,踢我,不,連我都殺:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他跟著你;出於愛我跟著他;但他把我趕走,威脅要打我,踢我,不,連我也殺:

passages.original: And now, so you will let me quiet go, To Athens will I bear my folly back, And follow you no further.
passages.vernacular: 而家,如果你讓我安靜地走,我就把我嘅愚蠢帶回雅典,唔再跟住你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,如果你讓我安靜地走,我就把我的愚蠢帶回雅典,不再跟著你。

passages.original: Let me go: You see how simple and how fond I am.
passages.vernacular: 讓我走:你睇我幾咁單純、幾咁癡情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我走:你看我多麼單純、多麼癡情。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Why, get you gone.
passages.vernacular: 哎,走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,走吧。

passages.original: Who is’t that hinders you?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺阻礙你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在阻礙你?

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: A foolish heart that I leave here behind.
passages.vernacular: 一顆愚蠢嘅心,我把佢留喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一顆愚蠢的心,我把它留在這裡。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: What!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼!

passages.original: with Lysander?
passages.vernacular: 同拉山德?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和拉山德?

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: With Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: 同狄米特律斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和狄米特律斯。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Be not afraid; she shall not harm thee, Helena.
passages.vernacular: 別怕;佢唔會傷害你,海倫娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別怕;她不會傷害你,海倫娜。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: No, sir, she shall not, though you take her part.
passages.vernacular: 不,先生,佢唔會,即使你幫佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,先生,她不會,即使你幫她。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: O, when she’s angry, she is keen and shrewd.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢生氣時,又尖銳又潑辣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,她生氣時,又尖銳又潑辣。

passages.original: She was a vixen when she went to school, And though she be but little, she is fierce.
passages.vernacular: 佢上學時就係頭悍婦,雖然佢好小,卻好兇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她上學時就是頭悍婦,雖然她很小,卻很兇。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Little again!
passages.vernacular: 又講小!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又說小!

passages.original: Nothing but low and little?
passages.vernacular: 除咗矮同小仲有乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了矮和小還有什麼?

passages.original: Why will you suffer her to flout me thus?
passages.vernacular: 你點解容許佢咁樣嘲弄我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼容許她這樣嘲弄我?

passages.original: Let me come to her.
passages.vernacular: 讓我去對付佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我去對付她。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Get you gone, you dwarf; You minimus, of hind’ring knot-grass made; You bead, you acorn.
passages.vernacular: 滾,你呢矮子;你呢個最小嘅嘢,用阻礙人嘅結縷草做嘅;你呢珠子,你呢橡果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾,你這矮子;你這最小的東西,用阻礙人的結縷草做的;你這珠子,你這橡果。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: You are too officious In her behalf that scorns your services.
passages.vernacular: 你對佢太殷勤喇,佢鄙視你嘅服務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對她太殷勤了,她鄙視你的服務。

passages.original: Let her alone.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓她一個人。

passages.original: Speak not of Helena; Take not her part; for if thou dost intend Never so little show of love to her, Thou shalt aby it.
passages.vernacular: 別提海倫娜;別幫佢;因為如果你對佢有邊怕啲愛嘅表示,你就得為此付出代價。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別提海倫娜;別幫她;因為如果你對她有哪怕一點愛的表示,你就得為此付出代價。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Now she holds me not.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢拉不住我喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在她拉不住我了。

passages.original: Now follow, if thou dar’st, to try whose right, Of thine or mine, is most in Helena.
passages.vernacular: 而家跟嚟,如果你敢,嚟試試你同我邊個對海倫娜嘅權利更大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在跟來,如果你敢,來試試你和我誰對海倫娜的權利更大。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Follow!
passages.vernacular: 跟嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟來!

passages.original: Nay, I’ll go with thee, cheek by jole.
passages.vernacular: 不,我跟你去,緊貼住你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我跟你去,緊貼著你。

passages.original: [Exeunt Lysander and Demetrius.]
passages.vernacular: [拉山德同狄米特律斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拉山德與狄米特律斯下。]

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: You, mistress, all this coil is long of you.
passages.vernacular: 你,小姐,呢一切混亂都因你而起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,小姐,這一切混亂都因你而起。

passages.original: Nay, go not back.
passages.vernacular: 不,別退回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,別退回去。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: I will not trust you, I, Nor longer stay in your curst company.
passages.vernacular: 我不信你,我唔再留喺你呢該死嘅同伴中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不信你,我不再留在你這該死的同伴中。

passages.original: Your hands than mine are quicker for a fray.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅手比我嘅更快出手打架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的手比我的更快出手打架。

passages.original: My legs are longer though, to run away.
passages.vernacular: 不過我嘅腿更長,能逃跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我的腿更長,能逃跑。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: I am amaz’d, and know not what to say.
passages.vernacular: 我驚呆喇,唔知道講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我驚呆了,不知道說什麼。

passages.original: [Exit, pursuing Helena.]
passages.vernacular: [追趕海倫娜下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [追趕海倫娜下。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: This is thy negligence: still thou mistak’st, Or else commit’st thy knaveries willfully.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係你嘅疏忽:你總是弄錯,否則就係你故意搞鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是你的疏忽:你總是弄錯,否則就是你故意搞鬼。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Believe me, king of shadows, I mistook.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,陰影之王,我弄錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,陰影之王,我弄錯了。

passages.original: Did not you tell me I should know the man By the Athenian garments he had on?
passages.vernacular: 你唔係告訴我,我能從嗰男人穿嘅雅典服裝認出佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是告訴我,我能從那男人穿的雅典服裝認出他嗎?

passages.original: And so far blameless proves my enterprise That I have ’nointed an Athenian’s eyes:
passages.vernacular: 到呢個程度,我嘅任務可算無罪,我已塗咗一個雅典人嘅眼睛:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到這個程度,我的任務可算無罪,我已塗了一個雅典人的眼睛:

passages.original: And so far am I glad it so did sort, As this their jangling I esteem a sport.
passages.vernacular: 到呢個程度,我好高興事情咁樣配成,我把佢哋嘅爭吵視為一場遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到這個程度,我很高興事情這樣配成,我把他們的爭吵視為一場遊戲。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Thou seest these lovers seek a place to fight.
passages.vernacular: 你睇呢啲戀人喺尋找決鬥嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看這些戀人在尋找決鬥的地方。

passages.original: Hie therefore, Robin, overcast the night; The starry welkin cover thou anon With drooping fog, as black as Acheron, And lead these testy rivals so astray As one come not within another’s way.
passages.vernacular: 所以快去,羅賓,使夜晚昏暗;即刻用低垂嘅霧、像阿刻戎一樣黑,遮蓋星空,領呢啲暴躁嘅情敵咁樣迷路,使其中一個唔會走到另一個嘅路上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以快去,羅賓,使夜晚昏暗;立刻用低垂的霧、像阿刻戎一樣黑,遮蓋星空,領這些暴躁的情敵這樣迷路,使其中一個不會走到另一個的路上。

passages.original: Like to Lysander sometime frame thy tongue, Then stir Demetrius up with bitter wrong;
passages.vernacular: 有時使你嘅舌頭像拉山德,用惡毒嘅冤屈激怒狄米特律斯;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時使你的舌頭像拉山德,用惡毒的冤屈激怒狄米特律斯;

passages.original: And sometime rail thou like Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: 有時又像狄米特律斯嗰樣叫罵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時又像狄米特律斯那樣叫罵。

passages.original: And from each other look thou lead them thus, Till o’er their brows death-counterfeiting sleep With leaden legs and batty wings doth creep.
passages.vernacular: 用呢種方式引佢哋各自遠離,直到像死亡般嘅瞓眠,用鉛一樣嘅腿同蝙蝠嘅翅膀,爬上佢哋嘅眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用這種方式引他們各自遠離,直到像死亡般的睡眠,用鉛一樣的腿和蝙蝠的翅膀,爬上他們的眉頭。

passages.original: Then crush this herb into Lysander’s eye, Whose liquor hath this virtuous property, To take from thence all error with his might And make his eyeballs roll with wonted sight.
passages.vernacular: 然後把呢種草搗碎喺拉山德眼裡,佢嘅汁液有咁樣嘅功效,把一切錯誤從嗰度全力取走,使佢嘅眼球恢復尋常嘅視力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後把這種草搗碎在拉山德眼裡,它的汁液有這樣的功效,把一切錯誤從那裡全力取走,使他的眼球恢復尋常的視力。

passages.original: When they next wake, all this derision Shall seem a dream and fruitless vision;
passages.vernacular: 等佢哋下次醒嚟,所有呢啲嘲笑都像係夢同無果嘅幻象;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他們下次醒來,所有這些嘲笑都像是夢和無果的幻象;

passages.original: And back to Athens shall the lovers wend, With league whose date till death shall never end.
passages.vernacular: 戀人哋將回雅典,結成同盟,其期限直到死亡都不終止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戀人們將回雅典,結成同盟,其期限直到死亡也不終止。

passages.original: Whiles I in this affair do thee employ, I’ll to my queen, and beg her Indian boy;
passages.vernacular: 當我喺呢件事上差遣你時,我要去找我嘅王后,向佢求佢嘅印度男孩;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我在這件事上差遣你時,我要去找我的王后,向她求她的印度男孩;

passages.original: And then I will her charmèd eye release From monster’s view, and all things shall be peace.
passages.vernacular: 然後我會把佢被魔法迷惑嘅眼睛從怪物嘅景象中釋放,一切都將平安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我會把她被魔法迷惑的眼睛從怪物的景象中釋放,一切都將平安。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: My fairy lord, this must be done with haste, For night’s swift dragons cut the clouds full fast;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅仙王,呢件事必須趕快做,因為夜嘅飛龍切開雲層好快;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的仙王,這件事必須趕快做,因為夜的飛龍切開雲層非常快;

passages.original: And yonder shines Aurora’s harbinger, At whose approach, ghosts wandering here and there Troop home to churchyards.
passages.vernacular: 嗰邊閃耀住黎明嘅先鋒,佢一靠近,四處遊蕩嘅鬼魂就成群回到墓地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那邊閃耀著黎明的先鋒,她一靠近,四處遊蕩的鬼魂就成群回到墓地。

passages.original: Damnèd spirits all, That in cross-ways and floods have burial, Already to their wormy beds are gone;
passages.vernacular: 所有被詛咒嘅靈魂,葬喺十字路口同水中嘅,已經回到佢哋蛆蟲嘅床上;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有被詛咒的靈魂,葬在十字路口和水中的,已經回到他們蛆蟲的床上;

passages.original: For fear lest day should look their shames upon, They wilfully themselves exile from light, And must for aye consort with black-brow’d night.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋怕白晝睇見佢哋嘅羞恥,故意把自己從光明中放逐,必須永遠同黑眉嘅夜為伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們怕白晝看見他們的羞恥,故意把自己從光明中放逐,必須永遠同黑眉的夜為伴。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: But we are spirits of another sort: I with the morning’s love have oft made sport;
passages.vernacular: 但我哋係另一類精靈:我常同晨嘅愛人嬉戲;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們是另一類精靈:我常與晨的愛人嬉戲;

passages.original: And, like a forester, the groves may tread Even till the eastern gate, all fiery-red, Opening on Neptune with fair blessèd beams, Turns into yellow gold his salt-green streams.
passages.vernacular: 像林務官一樣,可以喺樹林中行走,直到東方嘅大門,火紅一片,以美好蒙福嘅光束向海神打開,把佢鹹綠嘅水流變成黃金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像林務官一樣,可以在樹林中行走,直到東方的大門,火紅一片,以美好蒙福的光束向海神打開,把他鹹綠的水流變成黃金。

passages.original: But, notwithstanding, haste, make no delay.
passages.vernacular: 不過,無論如何,快,別耽擱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,無論如何,快,別耽擱。

passages.original: We may effect this business yet ere day.
passages.vernacular: 我哋仲能喺白天之前完成呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們還能在白天之前完成這件事。

passages.original: [Exit Oberon.]
passages.vernacular: [奧布朗下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧布朗下。]

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Up and down, up and down, I will lead them up and down.
passages.vernacular: 上上下下,上上下下,我要領佢哋上上下下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上上下下,上上下下,我要領他們上上下下。

passages.original: I am fear’d in field and town.
passages.vernacular: 田野同城鎮都怕我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 田野和城鎮都怕我。

passages.original: Goblin, lead them up and down.
passages.vernacular: 小妖,領佢哋上上下下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小妖,領他們上上下下。

passages.original: Here comes one.
passages.vernacular: 呢度嚟咗一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡來了一個。

passages.original: Enter Lysander.
passages.vernacular: [拉山德上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拉山德上。]

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Where art thou, proud Demetrius?
passages.vernacular: 你喺邊度,驕傲嘅狄米特律斯?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在哪裡,驕傲的狄米特律斯?

passages.original: Speak thou now.
passages.vernacular: 你而家講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在說話。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Here, villain, drawn and ready.
passages.vernacular: 呢度,惡棍,拔劍準備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡,惡棍,拔劍準備好。

passages.original: Where art thou?
passages.vernacular: 你喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在哪裡?

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: I will be with thee straight.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻就到你嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我馬上就到你那裡。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Follow me then to plainer ground.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就跟我到更平坦嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就跟我到更平坦的地方。

passages.original: [Exit Lysander as following the voice.]
passages.vernacular: [拉山德循聲下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拉山德循聲下。]

passages.original: Enter Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: [狄米特律斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [狄米特律斯上。]

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Lysander, speak again.
passages.vernacular: 拉山德,再講一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉山德,再說一次。

passages.original: Thou runaway, thou coward, art thou fled? Speak.
passages.vernacular: 你呢逃兵,你呢懦夫,你逃咗嗎?講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這逃兵,你這懦夫,你逃了嗎?說話。

passages.original: In some bush?
passages.vernacular: 喺某個灌木叢裡?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在某個灌木叢裡?

passages.original: Where dost thou hide thy head?
passages.vernacular: 你把頭藏喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把頭藏在哪裡?

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Thou coward, art thou bragging to the stars, Telling the bushes that thou look’st for wars, And wilt not come?
passages.vernacular: 你呢懦夫,你係喺對星星吹牛,對灌木叢講你喺找戰爭,卻不嚟嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這懦夫,你是在對星星吹牛,對灌木叢說你在找戰爭,卻不來嗎?

passages.original: Come, recreant, come, thou child!
passages.vernacular: 嚟,背信者,嚟,你呢細路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,背信者,來,你這孩子!

passages.original: I’ll whip thee with a rod.
passages.vernacular: 我要用棍子抽你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要用棍子抽你。

passages.original: He is defil’d That draws a sword on thee.
passages.vernacular: 向你拔劍嘅人會被玷污。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向你拔劍的人會被玷污。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Yea, art thou there?
passages.vernacular: 對,你喺嗰度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,你在那裡嗎?

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Follow my voice; we’ll try no manhood here.
passages.vernacular: 跟住我嘅聲音;我哋喺呢度不試男子氣概。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟著我的聲音;我們在這裡不試男子氣概。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

passages.original: Enter Lysander.
passages.vernacular: [拉山德上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拉山德上。]

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: He goes before me, and still dares me on; When I come where he calls, then he is gone.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺我前面走,仲一直向我挑戰;我到佢叫嘅地方,佢就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在我前面走,還一直向我挑戰;我到他叫的地方,他就走了。

passages.original: The villain is much lighter-heel’d than I: I follow’d fast, but faster he did fly, That fallen am I in dark uneven way, And here will rest me.
passages.vernacular: 嗰惡棍嘅腳跟比我輕快得多:我追得快,佢逃得更快,以致我喺黑暗崎嶇嘅路上跌倒,我就喺呢度休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那惡棍的腳跟比我輕快得多:我追得快,他逃得更快,以致我在黑暗崎嶇的路上跌倒,我就在這裡休息。

passages.original: Come, thou gentle day!
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,溫和嘅白日!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,溫和的白日!

passages.original: [Lies down.]
passages.vernacular: [躺下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [躺下。]

passages.original: For if but once thou show me thy grey light, I’ll find Demetrius, and revenge this spite.
passages.vernacular: 因為只要你向我顯現一次你嘅灰色光,我就會找到狄米特律斯,報呢個仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為只要你向我顯現一次你的灰色光,我就會找到狄米特律斯,報這個仇。

passages.original: [Sleeps.]
passages.vernacular: [入瞓。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [入睡。]

passages.original: Enter Puck and Demetrius.
passages.vernacular: [帕克同狄米特律斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [帕克與狄米特律斯上。]

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Ho, ho, ho!
passages.vernacular: 嗬,嗬,嗬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗬,嗬,嗬!

passages.original: Coward, why com’st thou not?
passages.vernacular: 懦夫,你點解不嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懦夫,你為什麼不來?

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Abide me, if thou dar’st; for well I wot Thou runn’st before me, shifting every place, And dar’st not stand, nor look me in the face.
passages.vernacular: 等我,如果你敢;因為我好清楚你喺我前面跑,變換每個地方,唔敢站住,都唔敢睇我嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我,如果你敢;因為我很清楚你在我前面跑,變換每個地方,不敢站住,也不敢看我的臉。

passages.original: Where art thou?
passages.vernacular: 你喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在哪裡?

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Come hither; I am here.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟;我喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來;我在這裡。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Nay, then, thou mock’st me.
passages.vernacular: 不,咁你係喺嘲弄我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,那麼你是在嘲弄我。

passages.original: Thou shalt buy this dear If ever I thy face by daylight see: Now go thy way.
passages.vernacular: 如果我白天見到你嘅臉,你要為此付出昂貴代價:而家走你嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我白天見到你的臉,你要為此付出昂貴代價:現在走你的路。

passages.original: Faintness constraineth me To measure out my length on this cold bed.
passages.vernacular: 疲倦迫使我喺呢冰冷嘅床上伸展身體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 疲倦迫使我在這冰冷的床上伸展身體。

passages.original: By day’s approach look to be visited.
passages.vernacular: 白天一到,等住被我拜訪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白天一到,等著被我拜訪。

passages.original: [Lies down and sleeps.]
passages.vernacular: [躺下入瞓。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [躺下入睡。]

passages.original: Enter Helena.
passages.vernacular: [海倫娜上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [海倫娜上。]

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: O weary night, O long and tedious night, Abate thy hours!
passages.vernacular: 啊疲憊嘅夜,啊漫長乏味嘅夜,縮短你嘅時辰吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊疲憊的夜,啊漫長乏味的夜,縮短你的時辰吧!

passages.original: Shine, comforts, from the east, That I may back to Athens by daylight, From these that my poor company detest.
passages.vernacular: 照耀吧,安慰,從東方嚟,好讓我藉日光回雅典,離開呢啲憎厭我可憐陪伴嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照耀吧,安慰,從東方來,好讓我藉日光回雅典,離開這些憎厭我可憐陪伴的人。

passages.original: And sleep, that sometimes shuts up sorrow’s eye, Steal me awhile from mine own company.
passages.vernacular: 仲有瞓眠,你有時合上悲傷嘅眼睛,把我從自己嘅陪伴中偷走一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有睡眠,你有時合上悲傷的眼睛,把我從自己的陪伴中偷走一會兒。

passages.original: [Sleeps.]
passages.vernacular: [入瞓。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [入睡。]

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Yet but three?
passages.vernacular: 才三個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 才三個?

passages.original: Come one more.
passages.vernacular: 再嚟一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再來一個。

passages.original: Two of both kinds makes up four.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男嘅兩個女嘅就湊足四個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男的兩個女的就湊足四個。

passages.original: Here she comes, curst and sad.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟喇,惱怒而悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她來了,惱怒而悲傷。

passages.original: Cupid is a knavish lad Thus to make poor females mad.
passages.vernacular: 丘比特係個頑皮嘅小子,咁樣使可憐嘅女人發瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 丘比特是個頑皮的小子,這樣使可憐的女人發瘋。

passages.original: Enter Hermia.
passages.vernacular: [赫米婭上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [赫米婭上。]

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Never so weary, never so in woe, Bedabbled with the dew, and torn with briers, I can no further crawl, no further go;
passages.vernacular: 從冇咁疲倦,從冇咁悲痛,被露水濺濕,被荊棘撕破,我唔能夠再爬,唔能夠再走;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從沒這麼疲倦,從沒這麼悲痛,被露水濺濕,被荊棘撕破,我不能再爬,不能再走;

passages.original: My legs can keep no pace with my desires.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅雙腿跟不上我嘅願望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的雙腿跟不上我的願望。

passages.original: Here will I rest me till the break of day.
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢度休息到天亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這裡休息到天亮。

passages.original: Heavens shield Lysander, if they mean a fray!
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋要打架,願上天保佑拉山德!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他們要打架,願上天保佑拉山德!

passages.original: [Lies down.]
passages.vernacular: [躺下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [躺下。]

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: On the ground Sleep sound.
passages.vernacular: 喺地上,瞓得沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在地上,睡得沉。

passages.original: I’ll apply To your eye, Gentle lover, remedy.
passages.vernacular: 我要用喺你眼上,溫柔嘅情人,補救。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要用在你眼上,溫柔的情人,補救。

passages.original: [Squeezing the juice on Lysander’s eye.]
passages.vernacular: [把汁液擠喺拉山德眼上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [把汁液擠在拉山德眼上。]

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: When thou wak’st, Thou tak’st True delight In the sight Of thy former lady’s eye.
passages.vernacular: 當你醒嚟,你會得到真正嘅歡樂,睇住你從前嘅小姐嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你醒來,你會得到真正的歡樂,看著你從前的小姐的眼睛。

passages.original: And the country proverb known, That every man should take his own, In your waking shall be shown:
passages.vernacular: 嗰句鄉村諺語眾所周知,每個人應當取回屬於自己嘅,喺你醒嚟時將要顯現:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那句鄉村諺語眾所周知,每個人應當取回屬於自己的,在你醒來時將要顯現:

passages.original: Jack shall have Jill; Nought shall go ill; The man shall have his mare again, and all shall be well.
passages.vernacular: 傑克配吉兒;冇乜嘢會出錯;男人將重新得回佢嘅母馬,一切都會好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑克配吉兒;沒有什麼會出錯;男人將重新得回他的母馬,一切都會好。

passages.original: [Exit Puck.]
passages.vernacular: [帕克下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [帕克下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene I — The Wood 第四幕第一場:樹林

passages.original: Lysander, Demetrius, Helena and Hermia still asleep.
passages.vernacular: [拉山德、狄米特律斯、海倫娜同赫米婭仍瞓住。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拉山德、狄米特律斯、海倫娜與赫米婭仍睡著。]

passages.original: Enter Titania and Bottom; Peaseblossom, Cobweb, Moth, Mustardseed and other Fairies attending; Oberon behind, unseen.
passages.vernacular: [蒂塔妮婭同波頓上;豆花、蛛網、飛蛾、芥子同其他仙子侍候;奧布朗喺後面,隱身。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [蒂塔妮婭與波頓上;豆花、蛛網、飛蛾、芥子與其他仙子侍候;奧布朗在後面,隱身。]

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Come, sit thee down upon this flowery bed, While I thy amiable cheeks do coy, And stick musk-roses in thy sleek smooth head, And kiss thy fair large ears, my gentle joy.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,坐喺呢花床上,我撫弄你可愛嘅臉頰,喺你光滑嘅頭上插麝香玫瑰,吻你美麗嘅大耳朵,我溫柔嘅歡喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,坐在這花床上,我撫弄你可愛的臉頰,在你光滑的頭上插麝香玫瑰,吻你美麗的大耳朵,我溫柔的歡喜。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Where’s Peaseblossom?
passages.vernacular: 豆花喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 豆花在哪裡?

passages.title: Peaseblossom 豆花
passages.original: Ready.
passages.vernacular: 喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Scratch my head, Peaseblossom.
passages.vernacular: 畀我搔頭,豆花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我搔頭,豆花。

passages.original: Where’s Monsieur Cobweb?
passages.vernacular: 蛛網先生喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蛛網先生在哪裡?

passages.title: Cobweb 蛛網
passages.original: Ready.
passages.vernacular: 喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Monsieur Cobweb; good monsieur, get you your weapons in your hand and kill me a red-hipped humble-bee on the top of a thistle;
passages.vernacular: 蛛網先生;好先生,攞起你嘅武器,替我殺一隻紅屁股嘅熊蜂,喺薊草頂上;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蛛網先生;好先生,拿起你的武器,替我殺一隻紅屁股的熊蜂,在薊草頂上;

passages.original: and, good monsieur, bring me the honey-bag.
passages.vernacular: 仲有,好先生,把蜜囊畀我攞嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,好先生,把蜜囊給我拿來。

passages.original: Do not fret yourself too much in the action, monsieur;
passages.vernacular: 先生,別喺行動中太焦急;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,別在行動中太焦急;

passages.original: and, good monsieur, have a care the honey-bag break not;
passages.vernacular: 仲有,好先生,小心別弄破蜜囊;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,好先生,小心別弄破蜜囊;

passages.original: I would be loath to have you overflown with a honey-bag, signior.
passages.vernacular: 我唔願見你被蜜囊淹沒,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不願見你被蜜囊淹沒,先生。

passages.original: Where’s Monsieur Mustardseed?
passages.vernacular: 芥子先生喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 芥子先生在哪裡?

passages.title: Mustardseed 芥子
passages.original: Ready.
passages.vernacular: 喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Give me your neaf, Monsieur Mustardseed.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅拳頭畀我,芥子先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的拳頭給我,芥子先生。

passages.original: Pray you, leave your courtesy, good monsieur.
passages.vernacular: 請你,別客氣喇,好先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,別客氣了,好先生。

passages.title: Mustardseed 芥子
passages.original: What’s your will?
passages.vernacular: 你有何吩咐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有何吩咐?

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Nothing, good monsieur, but to help Cavalery Cobweb to scratch.
passages.vernacular: 冇,好先生,只係幫騎士蛛網搔癢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,好先生,只是幫騎士蛛網搔癢。

passages.original: I must to the barber’s, monsieur, for methinks I am marvellous hairy about the face;
passages.vernacular: 我得去理髮店,先生,因為我覺得臉上毛茸茸嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得去理髮店,先生,因為我覺得臉上毛茸茸的;

passages.original: and I am such a tender ass, if my hair do but tickle me, I must scratch.
passages.vernacular: 我係咁嬌嫩嘅驢,只要毛髮一搔我,我就必須抓癢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是這麼嬌嫩的驢,只要毛髮一搔我,我就必須抓癢。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: What, wilt thou hear some music, my sweet love?
passages.vernacular: 點,你想聽點音樂嗎,我甜蜜嘅愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,你想聽點音樂嗎,我甜蜜的愛?

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: I have a reasonable good ear in music.
passages.vernacular: 我對音樂有相當好嘅耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對音樂有相當好的耳朵。

passages.original: Let us have the tongs and the bones.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋嚟鉗子同骨頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們來鉗子和骨頭。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Or say, sweet love, what thou desirest to eat.
passages.vernacular: 或者講,甜蜜嘅愛,你想食乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者說,甜蜜的愛,你想吃什麼。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Truly, a peck of provender; I could munch your good dry oats.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,一配克草料;我能嚼你嗰好乾燕麥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,一配克草料;我能嚼你那好乾燕麥。

passages.original: Methinks I have a great desire to a bottle of hay:
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我極想要一捆乾草:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我極想要一捆乾草:

passages.original: good hay, sweet hay, hath no fellow.
passages.vernacular: 好乾草,甜乾草,無同倫比。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好乾草,甜乾草,無與倫比。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: I have a venturous fairy that shall seek The squirrel’s hoard, and fetch thee new nuts.
passages.vernacular: 我有一個大膽嘅仙子,佢會去尋松鼠嘅貯藏,畀你取新鮮堅果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一個大膽的仙子,他會去尋松鼠的貯藏,給你取新鮮堅果。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: I had rather have a handful or two of dried peas.
passages.vernacular: 我寧可要一兩把乾豌豆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧可要一兩把乾豌豆。

passages.original: But, I pray you, let none of your people stir me;
passages.vernacular: 但係,求你,唔好畀你嘅人驚動我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,求你,別讓你的人驚動我;

passages.original: I have an exposition of sleep come upon me.
passages.vernacular: 我有一種瞓意要嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一種睡意要來了。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Sleep thou, and I will wind thee in my arms.
passages.vernacular: 你瞓吧,我把你繞喺我臂彎裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你睡吧,我把你繞在我臂彎裡。

passages.original: Fairies, be gone, and be all ways away.
passages.vernacular: 仙子哋,走開,四面八方都走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙子們,走開,四面八方都走開。

passages.original: So doth the woodbine the sweet honeysuckle Gently entwist, the female ivy so Enrings the barky fingers of the elm.
passages.vernacular: 就像忍冬輕輕纏繞甜蜜嘅金銀花,雌性嘅常春藤咁樣纏繞榆樹粗皮嘅手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像忍冬輕輕纏繞甜蜜的金銀花,雌性的常春藤這樣纏繞榆樹粗皮的手指。

passages.original: O, how I love thee!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我幾咁愛你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我多麼愛你!

passages.original: How I dote on thee!
passages.vernacular: 我幾咁迷戀你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我多麼迷戀你!

passages.original: [They sleep.]
passages.vernacular: [二人入瞓。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [二人入睡。]

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Oberon advances. Enter Puck.
passages.vernacular: 奧布朗上前。帕克上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧布朗上前。帕克上。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Welcome, good Robin.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,好羅賓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,好羅賓。

passages.original: Seest thou this sweet sight?
passages.vernacular: 你睇見呢甜蜜嘅景象嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看見這甜蜜的景象嗎?

passages.original: Her dotage now I do begin to pity.
passages.vernacular: 我開始可憐佢嘅癡迷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我開始可憐她的癡迷了。

passages.original: For, meeting her of late behind the wood, Seeking sweet favours for this hateful fool, I did upbraid her and fall out with her:
passages.vernacular: 因為最近喺樹林後面遇到佢,佢喺為呢可恨嘅傻瓜尋找甜美嘅恩惠,我責備佢,同佢吵咗架:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為最近在樹林後面遇到她,她在為這可恨的傻瓜尋找甜美的恩惠,我責備她,同她吵了架:

passages.original: For she his hairy temples then had rounded With coronet of fresh and fragrant flowers;
passages.vernacular: 因為佢嗰時用鮮花馨香嘅小冠圍住佢毛茸茸嘅太陽穴;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為她那時用鮮花馨香的小冠圍住他毛茸茸的太陽穴;

passages.original: And that same dew, which sometime on the buds Was wont to swell like round and orient pearls, Stood now within the pretty flouriets’ eyes, Like tears that did their own disgrace bewail.
passages.vernacular: 而嗰同一滴露水,有時喺花蕾上曾像圓潤東方嘅珍珠一樣膨脹,而家站喺可愛小花嘅眼睛裡,像為自己嘅屈辱而哭泣嘅淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而那同一滴露水,有時在花蕾上曾像圓潤東方的珍珠一樣膨脹,現在站在可愛小花的眼睛裡,像為自己的屈辱而哭泣的淚。

passages.original: When I had at my pleasure taunted her, And she in mild terms begg’d my patience, I then did ask of her her changeling child;
passages.vernacular: 當我隨心所欲地嘲弄佢,佢用溫和嘅言辭懇求我嘅耐心,我便向佢要佢換嚟嘅細路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我隨心所欲地嘲弄她,她用溫和的言辭懇求我的耐心,我便向她要她換來的孩子;

passages.original: Which straight she gave me, and her fairy sent To bear him to my bower in fairyland.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻交畀我,並派佢嘅仙子把佢送到我喺仙境嘅閨房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她立刻交給我,並派她的仙子把他送到我在仙境的閨房。

passages.original: And now I have the boy, I will undo This hateful imperfection of her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 而家我有咗細路,我要解除佢眼睛呢可恨嘅缺陷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我有了孩子,我要解除她眼睛這可恨的缺陷。

passages.original: And, gentle Puck, take this transformèd scalp From off the head of this Athenian swain, That he awaking when the other do, May all to Athens back again repair, And think no more of this night’s accidents But as the fierce vexation of a dream.
passages.vernacular: 溫和嘅帕克,把呢顆轉化嘅頭顱從呢個雅典鄉下人嘅頭上取下,好讓佢同其他人一起醒嚟時,可以都回雅典,唔再把今夜嘅事想成別嘅,只當成夢嘅猛烈煩擾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫和的帕克,把這顆轉化的頭顱從這個雅典鄉下人的頭上取下,好讓他與其他人一起醒來時,可以都回雅典,不再把今夜的事想成別的,只當成夢的猛烈煩擾。

passages.original: But first I will release the Fairy Queen.
passages.vernacular: 但我先要釋放仙后。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我先要釋放仙后。

passages.original: [Touching her eyes with an herb.]
passages.vernacular: [用草碰佢嘅眼睛。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [用草碰她的眼睛。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Be as thou wast wont to be; See as thou was wont to see.
passages.vernacular: 恢復你原來嘅樣子;像從前一樣睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恢復你原來的樣子;像從前一樣看。

passages.original: Dian’s bud o’er Cupid’s flower Hath such force and blessed power.
passages.vernacular: 狄安娜嘅花蕾壓倒丘比特嘅花,有咁樣嘅力量同蒙福嘅威力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄安娜的花蕾壓倒丘比特的花,有這樣的力量與蒙福的威力。

passages.original: Now, my Titania, wake you, my sweet queen.
passages.vernacular: 而家,我嘅蒂塔妮婭,醒嚟,我甜蜜嘅王后。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,我的蒂塔妮婭,醒來,我甜蜜的王后。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: My Oberon, what visions have I seen!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅奧布朗,我睇見咗乜嘢幻象!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的奧布朗,我看見了什麼幻象!

passages.original: Methought I was enamour’d of an ass.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我愛上咗一頭驢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我愛上了一頭驢。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: There lies your love.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅愛人就躺喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的愛人就躺在那裡。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: How came these things to pass?
passages.vernacular: 呢啲事係點發生嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些事是怎麼發生的?

passages.original: O, how mine eyes do loathe his visage now!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我嘅眼睛而家幾咁憎惡佢嘅面孔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我的眼睛現在多麼憎惡他的面孔!

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Silence awhile.—Robin, take off this head.
passages.vernacular: 安靜一會兒。——羅賓,把呢顆頭取下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜一會兒。——羅賓,把這顆頭取下。

passages.original: Titania, music call; and strike more dead Than common sleep, of all these five the sense.
passages.vernacular: 蒂塔妮婭,叫音樂嚟;使呢五個人嘅感官比平常嘅瞓眠更沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂塔妮婭,叫音樂來;使這五個人的感官比平常的睡眠更沉。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Music, ho, music, such as charmeth sleep.
passages.vernacular: 音樂,嗬,音樂,能迷惑瞓眠嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 音樂,嗬,音樂,能迷惑睡眠的那種。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Now when thou wak’st, with thine own fool’s eyes peep.
passages.vernacular: 而家你醒嚟時,用你自己傻瓜嘅眼睛窺睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你醒來時,用你自己傻瓜的眼睛窺看。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Sound, music.
passages.vernacular: 奏樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奏樂。

passages.original: [Still music.]
passages.vernacular: [靜靜嘅音樂。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [靜靜的音樂。]

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Come, my queen, take hands with me, And rock the ground whereon these sleepers be.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我嘅王后,同我牽手,搖動呢啲瞓者所在嘅地面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我的王后,和我牽手,搖動這些睡者所在的地面。

passages.original: Now thou and I are new in amity, And will tomorrow midnight solemnly Dance in Duke Theseus’ house triumphantly, And bless it to all fair prosperity:
passages.vernacular: 而家你我又同好喇,明晚午夜將莊嚴地喺忒修斯公爵家裡凱旋地跳舞,祝福佢一切美好興旺:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你我又和好了,明晚午夜將莊嚴地在忒修斯公爵家裡凱旋地跳舞,祝福它一切美好興旺:

passages.original: There shall the pairs of faithful lovers be Wedded, with Theseus, all in jollity.
passages.vernacular: 嗰度忠實嘅戀人哋將同忒修斯一同,喺歡樂中成婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡忠實的戀人們將與忒修斯一同,在歡樂中成婚。

passages.title: Puck 帕克
passages.original: Fairy king, attend and mark.
passages.vernacular: 仙王,留心聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙王,留心聽。

passages.original: I do hear the morning lark.
passages.vernacular: 我聽到晨間嘅雲雀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽到晨間的雲雀。

passages.title: Oberon 奧布朗
passages.original: Then, my queen, in silence sad, Trip we after night’s shade.
passages.vernacular: 咁,我嘅王后,喺悲傷嘅沉默中,跟隨夜嘅陰影掠去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,我的王后,在悲傷的沉默中,跟隨夜的陰影掠去。

passages.original: We the globe can compass soon, Swifter than the wand’ring moon.
passages.vernacular: 我哋可以好快繞過地球,比遊蕩嘅月亮仲快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們可以很快繞過地球,比遊蕩的月亮還快。

passages.title: Titania 蒂塔妮婭
passages.original: Come, my lord, and in our flight, Tell me how it came this night That I sleeping here was found With these mortals on the ground.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我嘅大人,喺我哋飛行時,告訴我今夜點會咁樣,我瞓喺呢度被發現,同呢啲凡人躺喺地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我的大人,在我們飛行時,告訴我今夜怎麼會這樣,我睡在這裡被發現,與這些凡人躺在地上。

passages.original: [Exeunt. Horns sound within.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。內有號角聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。內有號角聲。]

passages.original: Enter Theseus, Hippolyta, Egeus and Train.
passages.vernacular: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、伊吉斯同隨從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、伊吉斯與隨從上。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Go, one of you, find out the forester; For now our observation is perform’d;
passages.vernacular: 你哋去一個人,找出林務官;因為我哋嘅觀察已完成;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們去一個人,找出林務官;因為我們的觀察已完成;

passages.original: And since we have the vaward of the day, My love shall hear the music of my hounds.
passages.vernacular: 既然我哋搶喺白天前頭,我嘅愛人將聽我獵犬嘅音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然我們搶在白天前頭,我的愛人將聽我獵犬的音樂。

passages.original: Uncouple in the western valley; let them go.
passages.vernacular: 喺西邊山谷放開犬鏈;讓佢哋去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在西邊山谷放開犬鏈;讓它們去。

passages.original: Dispatch I say, and find the forester.
passages.vernacular: 快,我講,去找林務官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快,我說,去找林務官。

passages.original: [Exit an Attendant.]
passages.vernacular: [一位侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一位侍從下。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: We will, fair queen, up to the mountain’s top, And mark the musical confusion Of hounds and echo in conjunction.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要,美麗嘅王后,上山頂,聽獵犬同回聲協奏嘅音樂般嘅混亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要,美麗的王后,上山頂,聽獵犬與回聲協奏的音樂般的混亂。

passages.title: Hippolyta 希波呂忒
passages.original: I was with Hercules and Cadmus once, When in a wood of Crete they bay’d the bear With hounds of Sparta.
passages.vernacular: 我曾同赫拉克勒斯同卡德摩斯喺一起,喺克里特嘅一片樹林裡,用斯巴達獵犬圍住熊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾與赫拉克勒斯和卡德摩斯在一起,在克里特的一片樹林裡,用斯巴達獵犬圍住熊。

passages.original: Never did I hear Such gallant chiding; for, besides the groves, The skies, the fountains, every region near Seem’d all one mutual cry.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇聽過咁樣英勇嘅吠叫;因為,除咗樹林,天空、泉水、附近每個地區似乎都係一片互相應同嘅叫聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒聽過這樣英勇的吠叫;因為,除了樹林,天空、泉水、附近每個地區似乎都是一片互相應和的叫聲。

passages.original: I never heard So musical a discord, such sweet thunder.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇聽過咁樣悅耳嘅不和諧,咁樣甜美嘅雷鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒聽過這樣悅耳的不和諧,這樣甜美的雷鳴。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: My hounds are bred out of the Spartan kind, So flew’d, so sanded;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅獵犬係斯巴達種所育,有咁樣嘅垂頰,咁樣嘅沙色;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的獵犬是斯巴達種所育,有這樣的垂頰,這樣的沙色;

passages.original: and their heads are hung With ears that sweep away the morning dew;
passages.vernacular: 牠哋嘅頭上掛住能掃去晨露嘅耳朵;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們的頭上掛著能掃去晨露的耳朵;

passages.original: Crook-knee’d and dewlap’d like Thessalian bulls;
passages.vernacular: 膝彎彎曲,垂肉如色薩利嘅公牛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 膝彎彎曲,垂肉如色薩利的公牛;

passages.original: Slow in pursuit, but match’d in mouth like bells, Each under each.
passages.vernacular: 追逐緩慢,但吠聲配合如鐘,一個比一個低。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 追逐緩慢,但吠聲配合如鐘,一個比一個低。

passages.original: A cry more tuneable Was never holla’d to, nor cheer’d with horn, In Crete, in Sparta, nor in Thessaly.
passages.vernacular: 喺克里特、斯巴達或色薩利,從冇人呼喚、用號角鼓勵過更悅耳嘅叫聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在克里特、斯巴達或色薩利,從沒有人呼喚、用號角鼓勵過更悅耳的叫聲。

passages.original: Judge when you hear.—But, soft, what nymphs are these?
passages.vernacular: 聽時自己判斷。——但係,慢住,呢啲係乜嘢仙女?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽時自己判斷。——但是,慢著,這些是什麼仙女?

passages.title: Egeus 伊吉斯
passages.original: My lord, this is my daughter here asleep, And this Lysander;
passages.vernacular: 大人,呢個係我嘅女兒,瞓喺呢度,呢個係拉山德;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,這是我的女兒,睡在這裡,這是拉山德;

passages.original: this Demetrius is; This Helena, old Nedar’s Helena:
passages.vernacular: 呢個係狄米特律斯;呢個係海倫娜,老尼達嘅海倫娜:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是狄米特律斯;這是海倫娜,老尼達的海倫娜:

passages.original: I wonder of their being here together.
passages.vernacular: 我奇怪佢哋點會一起喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我奇怪他們怎麼會一起在這裡。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: No doubt they rose up early to observe The rite of May;
passages.vernacular: 無疑佢哋好早起嚟,為了觀睇五月嘅儀式;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無疑他們很早起來,為了觀看五月的儀式;

passages.original: and, hearing our intent, Came here in grace of our solemnity.
passages.vernacular: 並聽講咗我哋嘅意圖,為了向我哋嘅盛典致敬而嚟到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並聽說了我們的意圖,為了向我們的盛典致敬而來到這裡。

passages.original: But speak, Egeus; is not this the day That Hermia should give answer of her choice?
passages.vernacular: 但講,伊吉斯;今日唔係赫米婭該答覆佢選擇嘅日子嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但說,伊吉斯;今天不是赫米婭該答覆她選擇的日子嗎?

passages.title: Egeus 伊吉斯
passages.original: It is, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,大人。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Go, bid the huntsmen wake them with their horns.
passages.vernacular: 去,叫獵人哋用號角叫醒佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,叫獵人們用號角叫醒他們。

passages.original: Horns, and shout within. Demetrius, Lysander, Hermia and Helena wake and start up.
passages.vernacular: [內有號角同呼喊聲。狄米特律斯、拉山德、赫米婭同海倫娜醒嚟並跳起。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角和呼喊聲。狄米特律斯、拉山德、赫米婭與海倫娜醒來並跳起。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Good morrow, friends.
passages.vernacular: 早安,朋友哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,朋友們。

passages.original: Saint Valentine is past.
passages.vernacular: 聖瓦倫丁節已過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖瓦倫丁節已過。

passages.original: Begin these wood-birds but to couple now?
passages.vernacular: 呢啲林鳥而家才開始配對嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些林鳥現在才開始配對嗎?

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: Pardon, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒,大人。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: He and the rest kneel to Theseus.
passages.vernacular: [佢同其餘嘅人向忒修斯下跪。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [他與其餘的人向忒修斯下跪。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: I pray you all, stand up.
passages.vernacular: 我請你哋都起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請你們都起來。

passages.original: I know you two are rival enemies.
passages.vernacular: 我知道你哋兩人係情敵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道你們兩人是情敵。

passages.original: How comes this gentle concord in the world, That hatred is so far from jealousy To sleep by hate, and fear no enmity?
passages.vernacular: 呢溫和嘅和諧在世上點嚟嘅,使恨離嫉妒咁遠,以致喺恨旁瞓住,不怕敵意?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這溫和的和諧在世上怎麼來的,使恨離嫉妒這麼遠,以致在恨旁睡著,不怕敵意?

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: My lord, I shall reply amazedly, Half sleep, half waking;
passages.vernacular: 大人,我會迷迷糊糊地回答,半瞓半醒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我會迷迷糊糊地回答,半睡半醒;

passages.original: but as yet, I swear, I cannot truly say how I came here.
passages.vernacular: 但我發誓,到而家為止,我仲唔能夠真正講出我點嚟到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我發誓,到現在為止,我還不能真正說出我怎麼來到這裡。

passages.original: But, as I think (for truly would I speak) And now I do bethink me, so it is:
passages.vernacular: 但就我所想(因為我確實想講實話)而家我想起嚟喇,係咁樣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但就我所想(因為我確實想說實話)現在我想起來了,是這樣:

passages.original: I came with Hermia hither.
passages.vernacular: 我同赫米婭嚟到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我同赫米婭來到這裡。

passages.original: Our intent Was to be gone from Athens, where we might be Without the peril of the Athenian law.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅意圖係離開雅典,喺嗰度我哋可以免於雅典法律嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的意圖是離開雅典,在那裡我們可以免於雅典法律的危險。

passages.title: Egeus 伊吉斯
passages.original: Enough, enough, my lord; you have enough.
passages.vernacular: 夠喇,夠喇,大人;您聽夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夠了,夠了,大人;您聽夠了。

passages.original: I beg the law, the law upon his head.
passages.vernacular: 我請求法律,法律落喺佢頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請求法律,法律落在他頭上。

passages.original: They would have stol’n away, they would, Demetrius, Thereby to have defeated you and me:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋本想偷偷溜走,係嘅,狄米特律斯,借此挫敗你同我:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們本想偷偷溜走,是的,狄米特律斯,借此挫敗你和我:

passages.original: You of your wife, and me of my consent, Of my consent that she should be your wife.
passages.vernacular: 你失去你嘅妻子,我失去我嘅同意,我同意佢做你妻子嘅同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你失去你的妻子,我失去我的同意,我同意她做你妻子的同意。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: My lord, fair Helen told me of their stealth, Of this their purpose hither to this wood;
passages.vernacular: 大人,美麗嘅海倫告訴我佢哋偷跑嘅事,佢哋嚟呢樹林嘅計劃;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,美麗的海倫告訴我他們偷跑的事,他們來這樹林的計劃;

passages.original: And I in fury hither follow’d them, Fair Helena in fancy following me.
passages.vernacular: 我喺憤怒中追到呢度,美麗嘅海倫娜出於迷戀追住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在憤怒中追到這裡,美麗的海倫娜出於迷戀追著我。

passages.original: But, my good lord, I wot not by what power, (But by some power it is) my love to Hermia, Melted as the snow, seems to me now As the remembrance of an idle gaud Which in my childhood I did dote upon;
passages.vernacular: 但係,我嘅好大人,我唔知憑乜嘢力量(但必係憑某種力量),我對赫米婭嘅愛,像雪一樣融化,而家喺我睇來就像對一件閒置小玩意嘅記憶,嗰個係我童年曾經迷戀嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,我的好大人,我不知憑什麼力量(但必是憑某種力量),我對赫米婭的愛,像雪一樣融化,現在在我看來就像對一件閒置小玩意的記憶,那是我童年曾經迷戀的;

passages.original: And all the faith, the virtue of my heart, The object and the pleasure of mine eye, Is only Helena.
passages.vernacular: 而我心中所有嘅信義、美德,我眼睛嘅對象同樂趣,只有海倫娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我心中所有的信義、美德,我眼睛的對象和樂趣,只有海倫娜。

passages.original: To her, my lord, Was I betroth’d ere I saw Hermia.
passages.vernacular: 大人,喺我見到赫米婭之前,我已同佢訂婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,在我見到赫米婭之前,我已與她訂婚。

passages.original: But like a sickness did I loathe this food.
passages.vernacular: 但我像生病一樣厭惡呢食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我像生病一樣厭惡這食物。

passages.original: But, as in health, come to my natural taste, Now I do wish it, love it, long for it, And will for evermore be true to it.
passages.vernacular: 但像恢復健康,回到我天然嘅口味,而家我希望佢,愛佢,渴求佢,並將永遠對佢忠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但像恢復健康,回到我天然的口味,現在我希望它,愛它,渴求它,並將永遠對它忠實。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Fair lovers, you are fortunately met.
passages.vernacular: 美麗嘅戀人哋,你哋幸運地相遇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗的戀人們,你們幸運地相遇了。

passages.original: Of this discourse we more will hear anon.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事我哋稍後再多聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事我們稍後再多聽。

passages.original: Egeus, I will overbear your will; For in the temple, by and by with us, These couples shall eternally be knit.
passages.vernacular: 伊吉斯,我要駁回你嘅意願;因為喺神殿裡,不久就同我哋一起,呢啲對子將永遠結合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊吉斯,我要駁回你的意願;因為在神殿裡,不久就與我們一起,這些對子將永遠結合。

passages.original: And, for the morning now is something worn, Our purpos’d hunting shall be set aside.
passages.vernacular: 而且,既然早晨已過去啲,我哋原定嘅狩獵將擱置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,既然早晨已過去一些,我們原定的狩獵將擱置。

passages.original: Away with us to Athens.
passages.vernacular: 隨我哋回雅典。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨我們回雅典。

passages.original: Three and three, We’ll hold a feast in great solemnity.
passages.vernacular: 三對三對,我哋將隆重地舉辦宴會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三對三對,我們將隆重地舉辦宴會。

passages.original: Come, Hippolyta.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,希波呂忒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,希波呂忒。

passages.original: [Exeunt Theseus, Hippolyta, Egeus and Train.]
passages.vernacular: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、伊吉斯同隨從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、伊吉斯與隨從下。]

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: These things seem small and undistinguishable, Like far-off mountains turnèd into clouds.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲事睇起嚟渺小而難以分辨,像遠處嘅山變成咗雲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些事看起來渺小而難以分辨,像遠處的山變成了雲。

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Methinks I see these things with parted eye, When everything seems double.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我用分開嘅眼睛睇呢啲事,當一切似乎都係雙重嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我用分開的眼睛看這些事,當一切似乎都是雙重的。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: So methinks.
passages.vernacular: 我都咁樣覺得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也這樣覺得。

passages.original: And I have found Demetrius like a jewel, Mine own, and not mine own.
passages.vernacular: 我找到咗狄米特律斯,像一顆寶石,係我自己嘅,又唔係我自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我找到了狄米特律斯,像一顆寶石,是我自己的,又不是我自己的。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Are you sure That we are awake?
passages.vernacular: 你確定我哋係醒住嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你確定我們是醒著的嗎?

passages.original: It seems to me That yet we sleep, we dream.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我哋仲喺瞓,喺做夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我們還在睡,在做夢。

passages.original: Do not you think The Duke was here, and bid us follow him?
passages.vernacular: 你不覺得公爵頭先喺呢度,叫我哋跟住佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不覺得公爵剛才在這裡,叫我們跟著他嗎?

passages.title: Hermia 赫米婭
passages.original: Yea, and my father.
passages.vernacular: 對,仲有我父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,還有我父親。

passages.title: Helena 海倫娜
passages.original: And Hippolyta.
passages.vernacular: 仲有希波呂忒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有希波呂忒。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: And he did bid us follow to the temple.
passages.vernacular: 佢確實叫我哋跟到神殿去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他確實叫我們跟到神殿去。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: Why, then, we are awake: let’s follow him, And by the way let us recount our dreams.
passages.vernacular: 哎,咁我哋係醒住嘅:我哋跟住佢,一路上讓我哋回述我哋嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,那麼我們是醒著的:我們跟著他,一路上讓我們回述我們的夢。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: [Waking.]
passages.vernacular: [醒嚟。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [醒來。]

passages.original: When my cue comes, call me, and I will answer.
passages.vernacular: 輪到我嘅提示時,叫我,我就回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輪到我的提示時,叫我,我就回答。

passages.original: My next is ‘Most fair Pyramus.’ Heigh-ho!
passages.vernacular: 我下一句係「最美嘅皮拉姆斯」。嘿嗬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我下一句是「最美的皮拉姆斯」。嘿嗬!

passages.original: Peter Quince!
passages.vernacular: 彼得·昆斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得·昆斯!

passages.original: Flute, the bellows-mender!
passages.vernacular: 弗魯特,修風箱嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗魯特,修風箱的!

passages.original: Snout, the tinker! Starveling!
passages.vernacular: 斯諾特,補鍋匠!斯塔夫林!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾特,補鍋匠!斯塔夫林!

passages.original: God’s my life!
passages.vernacular: 天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!

passages.original: Stol’n hence, and left me asleep!
passages.vernacular: 偷偷溜走,把我留喺瞓夢中!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 偷偷溜走,把我留在睡夢中!

passages.original: I have had a most rare vision.
passages.vernacular: 我睇咗一個極稀有嘅幻象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看了一個極稀有的幻象。

passages.original: I have had a dream, past the wit of man to say what dream it was.
passages.vernacular: 我做咗一個夢,人嘅智慧都講不出嗰個係乜嘢夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我做了一個夢,人的智慧都說不出那是什麼夢。

passages.original: Man is but an ass if he go about to expound this dream.
passages.vernacular: 人如果去解釋呢個夢,就只係頭驢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人如果去解釋這個夢,就只是頭驢。

passages.original: Methought I was—there is no man can tell what.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我係——冇人講得出係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我是——沒有人說得出是什麼。

passages.original: Methought I was, and methought I had—but man is but a patched fool if he will offer to say what methought I had.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我係,我覺得我有——但人若敢講我覺得我有乜嘢,就只係個打補丁嘅傻瓜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我是,我覺得我有——但人若敢說我覺得我有什麼,就只是個打補丁的傻瓜。

passages.original: The eye of man hath not heard, the ear of man hath not seen, man’s hand is not able to taste, his tongue to conceive, nor his heart to report, what my dream was.
passages.vernacular: 人嘅眼睛冇聽過,人嘅耳朵冇睇過,人嘅手唔能夠嘗,舌頭唔能夠想,心都唔能夠報告我嘅夢係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人的眼睛沒有聽過,人的耳朵沒有看過,人的手不能嘗,舌頭不能想,心也不能報告我的夢是什麼。

passages.original: I will get Peter Quince to write a ballad of this dream:
passages.vernacular: 我要叫彼得·昆斯為呢個夢寫一首歌謠:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要叫彼得·昆斯為這個夢寫一首歌謠:

passages.original: it shall be called ‘Bottom’s Dream’, because it hath no bottom;
passages.vernacular: 佢要叫《波頓之夢》,因為佢冇底;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它要叫《波頓之夢》,因為它沒有底;

passages.original: and I will sing it in the latter end of a play, before the Duke.
passages.vernacular: 我要喺戲嘅末尾,喺公爵面前唱佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要在戲的末尾,在公爵面前唱它。

passages.original: Peradventure, to make it the more gracious, I shall sing it at her death.
passages.vernacular: 或者為了使佢更動人,我要喺佢死嘅時候唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許為了使它更動人,我要在她死的時候唱。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene II — Athens. A Room in Quince’s House 第四幕第二場:雅典,昆斯家一室

passages.original: Enter Quince, Flute, Snout and Starveling.
passages.vernacular: [昆斯、弗魯特、斯諾特同斯塔夫林上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [昆斯、弗魯特、斯諾特與斯塔夫林上。]

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Have you sent to Bottom’s house?
passages.vernacular: 你派人去波頓家咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你派人去波頓家了嗎?

passages.original: Is he come home yet?
passages.vernacular: 佢回家咗冇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回家了沒有?

passages.title: Starveling 斯塔夫林
passages.original: He cannot be heard of.
passages.vernacular: 聽唔到佢嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽不到他的消息。

passages.original: Out of doubt he is transported.
passages.vernacular: 毫無疑問佢被帶走咗(變喇)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 毫無疑問他被帶走了(變了)。

passages.title: Flute 弗魯特
passages.original: If he come not, then the play is marred.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢不嚟,戲就毀喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他不來,戲就毀了。

passages.original: It goes not forward, doth it?
passages.vernacular: 唔能夠進行,係吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不能進行,是吧?

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: It is not possible.
passages.vernacular: 唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可能。

passages.original: You have not a man in all Athens able to discharge Pyramus but he.
passages.vernacular: 全雅典你找唔到一個人能演皮拉姆斯,只有佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全雅典你找不到一個人能演皮拉姆斯,只有他。

passages.title: Flute 弗魯特
passages.original: No, he hath simply the best wit of any handicraft man in Athens.
passages.vernacular: 不,佢確實係雅典所有手藝人中最聰明嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他確實是雅典所有手藝人中最聰明的。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Yea, and the best person too, and he is a very paramour for a sweet voice.
passages.vernacular: 對,而且都係最好嘅人物,佢嘅甜美聲音真係情人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,而且也是最好的人物,他的甜美聲音真是情人。

passages.title: Flute 弗魯特
passages.original: You must say paragon.
passages.vernacular: 你必須講「楷模」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你必須說「楷模」。

passages.original: A paramour is, God bless us, a thing of naught.
passages.vernacular: 「情人」,上帝保佑我哋,係不好嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「情人」,上帝保佑我們,是不好的東西。

passages.original: Enter Snug.
passages.vernacular: [斯納格上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [斯納格上。]

passages.title: Snug 斯納格
passages.original: Masters, the Duke is coming from the temple, and there is two or three lords and ladies more married.
passages.vernacular: 各位,公爵從神殿回嚟喇,仲有兩三對貴族同夫人都結咗婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各位,公爵從神殿回來了,還有兩三對貴族和夫人也結了婚。

passages.original: If our sport had gone forward, we had all been made men.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋嘅遊戲能進行,我哋都發財喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們的遊戲能進行,我們都發財了。

passages.title: Flute 弗魯特
passages.original: O sweet bully Bottom!
passages.vernacular: 啊親愛嘅好夥計波頓!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊親愛的好夥計波頓!

passages.original: Thus hath he lost sixpence a day during his life;
passages.vernacular: 佢就咁樣一輩子失去咗每天六便士;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他就這樣一輩子失去了每天六便士;

passages.original: he could not have ’scaped sixpence a day.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔可能逃過每天六便士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不可能逃過每天六便士。

passages.original: An the Duke had not given him sixpence a day for playing Pyramus, I’ll be hanged.
passages.vernacular: 如果公爵不畀佢演皮拉姆斯每天六便士,我就上吊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果公爵不給他演皮拉姆斯每天六便士,我就上吊。

passages.original: He would have deserved it: sixpence a day in Pyramus, or nothing.
passages.vernacular: 佢本會應得嘅:演皮拉姆斯,每天六便士,否則乜嘢都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他本會應得的:演皮拉姆斯,每天六便士,否則什麼都沒有。

passages.original: Enter Bottom.
passages.vernacular: [波頓上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [波頓上。]

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Where are these lads?
passages.vernacular: 呢啲小子喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些小子在哪裡?

passages.original: Where are these hearts?
passages.vernacular: 呢啲好漢喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些好漢在哪裡?

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Bottom!
passages.vernacular: 波頓!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波頓!

passages.original: O most courageous day!
passages.vernacular: 啊最勇敢嘅日子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊最勇敢的日子!

passages.original: O most happy hour!
passages.vernacular: 啊最幸福嘅時辰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊最幸福的時辰!

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Masters, I am to discourse wonders: but ask me not what;
passages.vernacular: 各位,我要談奇事:但別問我係乜嘢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各位,我要談奇事:但別問我是什麼;

passages.original: for if I tell you, I am not true Athenian.
passages.vernacular: 因為如果我告訴你哋,我就唔係真正嘅雅典人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果我告訴你們,我就不是真正的雅典人。

passages.original: I will tell you everything, right as it fell out.
passages.vernacular: 我會告訴你哋一切,恰如其發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會告訴你們一切,恰如其發生。

passages.title: Quince 昆斯
passages.original: Let us hear, sweet Bottom.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋聽聽,親愛嘅波頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們聽聽,親愛的波頓。

passages.title: Bottom 波頓
passages.original: Not a word of me.
passages.vernacular: 我一個字都不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一個字也不說。

passages.original: All that I will tell you is, that the Duke hath dined.
passages.vernacular: 我要告訴你哋嘅只係,公爵已經食過飯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要告訴你們的只是,公爵已經吃過飯了。

passages.original: Get your apparel together, good strings to your beards, new ribbons to your pumps;
passages.vernacular: 把你哋嘅服裝收拾好,鬍子上要有好繩子,舞鞋上要有新絲帶;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你們的服裝收拾好,鬍子上要有好繩子,舞鞋上要有新絲帶;

passages.original: meet presently at the palace; every man look o’er his part.
passages.vernacular: 即刻到宮裡會合;每個人睇一遍自己嘅台詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上到宮裡會合;每個人看一遍自己的台詞。

passages.original: For the short and the long is, our play is preferred.
passages.vernacular: 長話短講就係,我哋嘅戲被選中喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 長話短說就是,我們的戲被選中了。

passages.original: In any case, let Thisbe have clean linen; and let not him that plays the lion pare his nails, for they shall hang out for the lion’s claws.
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,讓提斯柏有乾淨嘅亞麻布;演獅子嘅別修指甲,因為佢哋要露出嚟當獅子嘅爪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,讓提斯柏有乾淨的亞麻布;演獅子的別修指甲,因為它們要露出來當獅子的爪。

passages.original: And most dear actors, eat no onions nor garlick, for we are to utter sweet breath;
passages.vernacular: 仲有最親愛嘅演員哋,別食洋蔥或大蒜,因為我哋要吐出甜美嘅氣息;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有最親愛的演員們,別吃洋蔥或大蒜,因為我們要吐出甜美的氣息;

passages.original: and I do not doubt but to hear them say it is a sweet comedy.
passages.vernacular: 我毫不懷疑會聽到佢哋講呢個係一齣甜美嘅喜劇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我毫不懷疑會聽到他們說這是一齣甜美的喜劇。

passages.original: No more words. Away! Go, away!
passages.vernacular: 唔使再講喇。走!去,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用再說了。走!去,走!

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act V, Scene I — Athens. An Apartment in the Palace of Theseus 第五幕第一場:雅典,忒修斯宮中一室

passages.original: Enter Theseus, Hippolyta, Philostrate, Lords and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、菲羅斯特拉特、眾貴族同侍從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [忒修斯、希波呂忒、菲羅斯特拉特、眾貴族與侍從上。]

passages.title: Hippolyta 希波呂忒
passages.original: ’Tis strange, my Theseus, that these lovers speak of.
passages.vernacular: 忒修斯,呢啲戀人哋講嘅事真奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 忒修斯,這些戀人們說的事真奇怪。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: More strange than true.
passages.vernacular: 奇怪多於真實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇怪多於真實。

passages.original: I never may believe These antique fables, nor these fairy toys.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔能夠相信呢啲古老嘅寓言,同呢啲仙子嘅玩意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不能相信這些古老的寓言,和這些仙子的玩意。

passages.original: Lovers and madmen have such seething brains, Such shaping fantasies, that apprehend More than cool reason ever comprehends.
passages.vernacular: 戀人同瘋子頭腦咁樣沸騰,咁樣塑造幻想,理解嘅比冷靜嘅理智所能理解嘅更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戀人和瘋子頭腦這樣沸騰,這樣塑造幻想,理解的比冷靜的理智所能理解的更多。

passages.original: The lunatic, the lover, and the poet Are of imagination all compact:
passages.vernacular: 瘋子、戀人同詩人,全都係想像力凝成嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瘋子、戀人和詩人,全都是想像力凝成的:

passages.original: One sees more devils than vast hell can hold;
passages.vernacular: 一個人睇見嘅魔鬼比廣闊嘅地獄所能容納嘅仲多;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人看見的魔鬼比廣闊的地獄所能容納的還多;

passages.original: That is the madman: the lover, all as frantic, Sees Helen’s beauty in a brow of Egypt:
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係瘋子:戀人,同樣狂亂,喺埃及人嘅額頭上睇見海倫嘅美:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是瘋子:戀人,同樣狂亂,在埃及人的額頭上看見海倫的美:

passages.original: The poet’s eye, in a fine frenzy rolling, Doth glance from heaven to earth, from earth to heaven;
passages.vernacular: 詩人嘅眼睛,喺美好嘅狂熱中轉動,從天堂瞥向大地,從大地瞥向天堂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詩人的眼睛,在美好的狂熱中轉動,從天堂瞥向大地,從大地瞥向天堂;

passages.original: And as imagination bodies forth The forms of things unknown, the poet’s pen Turns them to shapes, and gives to airy nothing A local habitation and a name.
passages.vernacular: 當想像力把未知事物嘅形狀賦予形體,詩人嘅筆把佢哋變成形狀,畀空虛嘅虛無一個地方嘅居所同一個名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當想像力把未知事物的形狀賦予形體,詩人的筆把它們變成形狀,給空虛的虛無一個地方的居所和一個名字。

passages.original: Such tricks hath strong imagination, That if it would but apprehend some joy, It comprehends some bringer of that joy.
passages.vernacular: 強烈嘅想像力有呢種把戲,只要佢想領悟某種歡樂,就領悟到一個帶嚟嗰歡樂嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 強烈的想像力有這種把戲,只要它想領悟某種歡樂,就領悟到一個帶來那歡樂的人。

passages.original: Or in the night, imagining some fear, How easy is a bush supposed a bear?
passages.vernacular: 或者喺夜裡,想像某種恐懼,把一叢灌木當成熊,幾咁容易?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者在夜裡,想像某種恐懼,把一叢灌木當成熊,多麼容易?

passages.title: Hippolyta 希波呂忒
passages.original: But all the story of the night told over, And all their minds transfigur’d so together, More witnesseth than fancy’s images, And grows to something of great constancy;
passages.vernacular: 但整夜嘅故事複述一遍,而且佢哋嘅心思咁樣一起變形,比幻想嘅影像更有見證力,並成為某種極穩定嘅嘢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但整夜的故事複述一遍,而且他們的心思這樣一起變形,比幻想的影像更有見證力,並成為某種極穩定的東西;

passages.original: But, howsoever, strange and admirable.
passages.vernacular: 但無論如何,係奇怪而令人驚嘆嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但無論如何,是奇怪而令人驚嘆的。

passages.original: Enter lovers: Lysander, Demetrius, Hermia and Helena.
passages.vernacular: [戀人哋:拉山德、狄米特律斯、赫米婭同海倫娜上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [戀人們:拉山德、狄米特律斯、赫米婭與海倫娜上。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Here come the lovers, full of joy and mirth.
passages.vernacular: 戀人哋嚟喇,滿係歡喜同快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戀人們來了,滿是歡喜與快樂。

passages.original: Joy, gentle friends, joy and fresh days of love Accompany your hearts!
passages.vernacular: 歡樂,溫和嘅朋友哋,歡樂同愛情清新嘅日子,伴隨你哋嘅心!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡樂,溫和的朋友們,歡樂和愛情清新的日子,伴隨你們的心!

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: More than to us Wait in your royal walks, your board, your bed!
passages.vernacular: 願比畀我哋嘅更多,喺你哋嘅御園、你哋嘅餐桌、你哋嘅床上等候住你哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願比給我們的更多,在你們的御園、你們的餐桌、你們的床上等候著你們!

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Come now; what masques, what dances shall we have, To wear away this long age of three hours Between our after-supper and bed-time?
passages.vernacular: 嚟,而家;我哋要有乜嘢化裝舞會、乜嘢舞蹈,嚟消磨我哋晚飯後到瞓覺前呢三個小時嘅漫長歲月?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,現在;我們要有什麼化裝舞會、什麼舞蹈,來消磨我們晚飯後到睡覺前這三個小時的漫長歲月?

passages.original: Where is our usual manager of mirth?
passages.vernacular: 我哋平時嘅歡樂總管喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們平時的歡樂總管在哪裡?

passages.original: What revels are in hand?
passages.vernacular: 有乜嘢歡樂節目準備好喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有什麼歡樂節目準備好了?

passages.original: Is there no play To ease the anguish of a torturing hour?
passages.vernacular: 冇戲嚟緩解一小時嘅折磨之苦嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有戲來緩解一小時的折磨之苦嗎?

passages.original: Call Philostrate.
passages.vernacular: 叫菲羅斯特拉特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫菲羅斯特拉特。

passages.title: Philostrate 菲羅斯特拉特
passages.original: Here, mighty Theseus.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,強大嘅忒修斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,強大的忒修斯。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Say, what abridgment have you for this evening?
passages.vernacular: 講,你為今晚準備咗乜嘢消遣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說,你為今晚準備了什麼消遣?

passages.original: What masque? What music?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢化裝舞?乜嘢音樂?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼化裝舞?什麼音樂?

passages.original: How shall we beguile The lazy time, if not with some delight?
passages.vernacular: 如果冇啲歡樂,我哋點樣打發呢遲緩嘅時光?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果沒有一些歡樂,我們怎樣打發這遲緩的時光?

passages.title: Philostrate 菲羅斯特拉特
passages.original: There is a brief how many sports are ripe.
passages.vernacular: 有一份簡表,列咗多少遊戲已準備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一份簡表,列了多少遊戲已準備好。

passages.original: Make choice of which your Highness will see first.
passages.vernacular: 請殿下選擇先睇邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請殿下選擇先看哪個。

passages.original: [Giving a paper.]
passages.vernacular: [遞上一張紙。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [遞上一張紙。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: [Reads] ‘The battle with the Centaurs, to be sung By an Athenian eunuch to the harp.’
passages.vernacular: [讀]「同半人馬嘅戰鬥,由一位雅典閹人伴住豎琴歌唱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: [讀]「與半人馬的戰鬥,由一位雅典閹人伴著豎琴歌唱。」

passages.original: We’ll none of that.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔好嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不要那個。

passages.original: That have I told my love In glory of my kinsman Hercules.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個我已為了榮耀我嘅親戚赫拉克勒斯告訴過我嘅愛人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個我已為了榮耀我的親戚赫拉克勒斯告訴過我的愛人。

passages.original: ‘The riot of the tipsy Bacchanals, Tearing the Thracian singer in their rage?’
passages.vernacular: 「醉酒嘅酒神女信徒喺盛怒中撕碎色雷斯歌手嘅喧鬧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「醉酒的酒神女信徒在盛怒中撕碎色雷斯歌手的喧鬧?」

passages.original: That is an old device, and it was play’d When I from Thebes came last a conqueror.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個老把戲,我上次從底比斯凱旋歸嚟時就演過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個老把戲,我上次從底比斯凱旋歸來時就演過。

passages.original: ‘The thrice three Muses mourning for the death Of learning, late deceas’d in beggary.’
passages.vernacular: 「三乘三位繆斯為最近喺乞討中去世嘅學問而哀悼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「三乘三位繆斯為最近在乞討中去世的學問而哀悼。」

passages.original: That is some satire, keen and critical, Not sorting with a nuptial ceremony.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係某種尖銳、批判嘅諷刺,不適合婚禮儀式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是某種尖銳、批判的諷刺,不適合婚禮儀式。

passages.original: ‘A tedious brief scene of young Pyramus And his love Thisbe; very tragical mirth.’
passages.vernacular: 「年輕嘅皮拉姆斯同佢嘅愛人提斯柏嘅一場冗長而簡短嘅劇;好悲劇嘅歡樂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「年輕的皮拉姆斯和他的愛人提斯柏的一場冗長而簡短的劇;非常悲劇的歡樂。」

passages.original: Merry and tragical?
passages.vernacular: 歡樂而悲劇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡樂而悲劇?

passages.original: Tedious and brief?
passages.vernacular: 冗長而簡短?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冗長而簡短?

passages.original: That is hot ice and wondrous strange snow.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係熱冰同奇妙嘅黑雪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是熱冰和奇妙的黑雪。

passages.original: How shall we find the concord of this discord?
passages.vernacular: 我哋點樣找到呢不和諧嘅和諧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們怎樣找到這不和諧的和諧?

passages.title: Philostrate 菲羅斯特拉特
passages.original: A play there is, my lord, some ten words long, Which is as brief as I have known a play;
passages.vernacular: 大人,有一齣戲大約十個字長,係我知道嘅最簡短嘅戲;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,有一齣戲大約十個字長,是我知道的最簡短的戲;

passages.original: But by ten words, my lord, it is too long, Which makes it tedious.
passages.vernacular: 但佢長咗十個字,大人,呢使佢冗長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它長了十個字,大人,這使它冗長。

passages.original: For in all the play There is not one word apt, one player fitted.
passages.vernacular: 因為整齣戲裡冇一個字合適,冇一個演員稱職。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為整齣戲裡沒有一個字合適,沒有一個演員稱職。

passages.original: And tragical, my noble lord, it is.
passages.vernacular: 佢係悲劇,我高貴嘅大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是悲劇,我高貴的大人。

passages.original: For Pyramus therein doth kill himself, Which, when I saw rehears’d, I must confess, Made mine eyes water;
passages.vernacular: 因為皮拉姆斯喺其中自殺,我睇排練時,必須承認,呢使我嘅眼睛流淚;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為皮拉姆斯在其中自殺,我看排練時,必須承認,這使我的眼睛流淚;

passages.original: but more merry tears The passion of loud laughter never shed.
passages.vernacular: 但更歡樂嘅淚,從冇大笑嘅激情流過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但更歡樂的淚,從沒有大笑的激情流過。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: What are they that do play it?
passages.vernacular: 演佢嘅係乜嘢人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 演它的是什麼人?

passages.title: Philostrate 菲羅斯特拉特
passages.original: Hard-handed men that work in Athens here, Which never labour’d in their minds till now;
passages.vernacular: 喺雅典呢度勞動嘅硬手男人,佢哋直到而家從冇用過腦子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在雅典這裡勞動的硬手男人,他們直到現在從沒用過腦子;

passages.original: And now have toil’d their unbreath’d memories With this same play against your nuptial.
passages.vernacular: 而家用冇訓練過嘅記憶,為您嘅婚禮辛苦地背呢齣戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在用沒訓練過的記憶,為您的婚禮辛苦地背這齣戲。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: And we will hear it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要聽。

passages.title: Philostrate 菲羅斯特拉特
passages.original: No, my noble lord, It is not for you: I have heard it over, And it is nothing, nothing in the world;
passages.vernacular: 不,我高貴嘅大人,呢不適合您:我聽完喇,乜嘢都唔係,世上乜嘢都唔係;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我高貴的大人,這不適合您:我聽完了,什麼也不是,世上什麼也不是;

passages.original: Unless you can find sport in their intents, Extremely stretch’d and conn’d with cruel pain To do you service.
passages.vernacular: 除非您能喺佢哋意圖中找到樂趣,佢哋為了服侍您,極度勉強地、帶住殘酷痛苦記熟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除非您能在他們意圖中找到樂趣,他們為了服侍您,極度勉強地、帶著殘酷痛苦記熟了。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: I will hear that play; For never anything can be amiss When simpleness and duty tender it.
passages.vernacular: 我要聽嗰齣戲;因為當單純同職責呈獻時,從來唔會有任何不妥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要聽那齣戲;因為當單純和職責呈獻時,從來不會有任何不妥。

passages.original: Go, bring them in: and take your places, ladies.
passages.vernacular: 去,把佢哋帶進嚟:各位女士,請就座。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,把他們帶進來:各位女士,請就座。

passages.original: [Exit Philostrate.]
passages.vernacular: [菲羅斯特拉特下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [菲羅斯特拉特下。]

passages.title: Hippolyta 希波呂忒
passages.original: I love not to see wretchedness o’ercharged, And duty in his service perishing.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意睇過度勉強嘅可憐,同盡職而喺服侍中衰竭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡看過度勉強的可憐,和盡職而在服侍中衰竭。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Why, gentle sweet, you shall see no such thing.
passages.vernacular: 哎,溫柔甜美嘅人,你唔會睇到嗰樣嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,溫柔甜美的人,你不會看到那樣的事。

passages.title: Hippolyta 希波呂忒
passages.original: He says they can do nothing in this kind.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢哋喺呢方面乜嘢都做不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他們在這方面什麼都做不了。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: The kinder we, to give them thanks for nothing.
passages.vernacular: 我哋更該仁慈,為佢哋乜嘢都冇做而道謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們更該仁慈,為他們什麼都沒做而道謝。

passages.original: Our sport shall be to take what they mistake:
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅遊戲就係採納佢哋嘅失誤:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的遊戲就是採納他們的失誤:

passages.original: And what poor duty cannot do, noble respect Takes it in might, not merit.
passages.vernacular: 凡可憐嘅職責所唔能夠做嘅,高貴嘅敬意就按誠意,不按功績接受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡可憐的職責所不能做的,高貴的敬意就按誠意,不按功績接受。

passages.original: Where I have come, great clerks have purposed To greet me with premeditated welcomes;
passages.vernacular: 我所到之處,大學者哋曾打算用事先準備嘅歡迎辭向我致意;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我所到之處,大學者們曾打算用事先準備的歡迎辭向我致意;

passages.original: Where I have seen them shiver and look pale, Make periods in the midst of sentences, Throttle their practis’d accent in their fears, And, in conclusion, dumbly have broke off, Not paying me a welcome.
passages.vernacular: 我睇見佢哋顫抖、臉色蒼白,喺句子中間停頓,喺恐懼中扼住佢哋練習過嘅腔調,最後啞然中斷,冇向我致歡迎辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看見他們顫抖、臉色蒼白,在句子中間停頓,在恐懼中扼住他們練習過的腔調,最後啞然中斷,沒有向我致歡迎辭。

passages.original: Trust me, sweet, Out of this silence yet I pick’d a welcome;
passages.vernacular: 相信我,甜心,我定係從呢沉默中拾起咗歡迎;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,甜心,我還是從這沉默中拾起了歡迎;

passages.original: And in the modesty of fearful duty I read as much as from the rattling tongue Of saucy and audacious eloquence.
passages.vernacular: 喺驚恐嘅職責嘅謙遜裡,我讀到嘅同從輕率放肆嘅口才嘅喋喋不休中讀到嘅一樣多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在驚恐的職責的謙遜裡,我讀到的和從輕率放肆的口才的喋喋不休中讀到的一樣多。

passages.original: Love, therefore, and tongue-tied simplicity In least speak most to my capacity.
passages.vernacular: 所以愛,同講不出話嘅單純,喺最少時講得最多,最合我嘅領悟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以愛,和說不出話的單純,在最少時說得最多,最合我的領悟。

passages.original: Enter Philostrate.
passages.vernacular: [菲羅斯特拉特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [菲羅斯特拉特上。]

passages.title: Philostrate 菲羅斯特拉特
passages.original: So please your grace, the Prologue is address’d.
passages.vernacular: 請殿下恩准,開場白已準備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請殿下恩准,開場白已準備好。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Let him approach.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢上前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他上前。

passages.original: Flourish of trumpets. Enter the Prologue.
passages.vernacular: [號角齊鳴。序幕者上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [號角齊鳴。序幕者上。]

passages.title: Prologue 序幕者
passages.original: If we offend, it is with our good will.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋冒犯,係出於我哋嘅好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們冒犯,是出於我們的好意。

passages.original: That you should think, we come not to offend, But with good will.
passages.vernacular: 您哋應該認為,我哋唔係為冒犯而嚟,而係出於好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您們應該認為,我們不是為冒犯而來,而是出於好意。

passages.original: To show our simple skill, That is the true beginning of our end.
passages.vernacular: 展示我哋嘅簡單技藝,呢個係我哋結束嘅真正開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 展示我們的簡單技藝,這是我們結束的真正開始。

passages.original: Consider then, we come but in despite.
passages.vernacular: 所以請想想,我哋嚟只係出於怨恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以請想想,我們來只是出於怨恨。

passages.original: We do not come, as minding to content you, Our true intent is.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嚟並唔係打算使您哋滿意,我哋真正嘅意圖係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們來並不是打算使您們滿意,我們真正的意圖是。

passages.original: All for your delight We are not here.
passages.vernacular: 為了您哋嘅歡樂,我哋不喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了您們的歡樂,我們不在這裡。

passages.original: That you should here repent you, The actors are at hand, and, by their show, You shall know all that you are like to know.
passages.vernacular: 為使您哋喺呢度後悔,演員就喺手邊,從佢哋嘅表演,您哋會知道一切您哋可能知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為使您們在這裡後悔,演員就在手邊,從他們的表演,您們會知道一切您們可能知道的。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: This fellow doth not stand upon points.
passages.vernacular: 呢傢伙不在意標點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這傢伙不在意標點。

passages.title: Lysander 拉山德
passages.original: He hath rid his prologue like a rough colt; he knows not the stop.
passages.vernacular: 佢像騎野小馬一樣念完咗佢嘅開場白;佢唔知道停頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他像騎野小馬一樣念完了他的開場白;他不知道停頓。

passages.original: A good moral, my lord: it is not enough to speak, but to speak true.
passages.vernacular: 一個好教訓,大人:光講話唔夠,要講得準確。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個好教訓,大人:光說話不夠,要說得準確。

passages.title: Hippolyta 希波呂忒
passages.original: Indeed he hath played on this prologue like a child on a recorder;
passages.vernacular: 確實佢演呢篇開場白,像細路吹豎笛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實他演這篇開場白,像孩子吹豎笛;

passages.original: a sound, but not in government.
passages.vernacular: 有聲音,但不受控制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有聲音,但不受控制。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: His speech was like a tangled chain; nothing impaired, but all disordered.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅話像一條纏結嘅鏈子;冇損壞,卻一團糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的話像一條纏結的鏈子;沒有損壞,卻一團糟。

passages.original: Who is next?
passages.vernacular: 下一個係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一個是誰?

passages.original: Enter Pyramus and Thisbe, Wall, Moonshine and Lion as in dumb show.
passages.vernacular: [皮拉姆斯同提斯柏、牆、月光同獅子,以啞劇方式上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [皮拉姆斯與提斯柏、牆、月光與獅子,以啞劇方式上。]

passages.title: Prologue 序幕者
passages.original: Gentles, perchance you wonder at this show; But wonder on, till truth make all things plain.
passages.vernacular: 各位,或者你哋對呢場表演感到驚奇;不過驚奇下去,直到真相使一切分明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各位,也許你們對這場表演感到驚奇;不過驚奇下去,直到真相使一切分明。

passages.original: This man is Pyramus, if you would know; This beauteous lady Thisbe is certain.
passages.vernacular: 呢個人係皮拉姆斯,如果你哋想知道;呢位美麗嘅小姐肯定係提斯柏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個人是皮拉姆斯,如果你們想知道;這位美麗的小姐肯定是提斯柏。

passages.original: This man, with lime and rough-cast, doth present Wall, that vile wall which did these lovers sunder;
passages.vernacular: 呢個人,帶住石灰同粗灰漿,扮演牆,嗰堵拆散呢對戀人嘅可恨嘅牆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個人,帶著石灰和粗灰漿,扮演牆,那堵拆散這對戀人的可恨的牆;

passages.original: And through Wall’s chink, poor souls, they are content To whisper, at the which let no man wonder.
passages.vernacular: 透過牆縫,可憐嘅靈魂哋樂意低聲講話,對此邊個都唔使驚奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 透過牆縫,可憐的靈魂們樂意低聲說話,對此誰也不用驚奇。

passages.original: This man, with lantern, dog, and bush of thorn, Presenteth Moonshine, for, if you will know, By moonshine did these lovers think no scorn To meet at Ninus’ tomb, there, there to woo.
passages.vernacular: 呢個人,帶住燈籠、狗同荊棘叢,扮演月光,因為,如果你哋想知道,就係喺月光下,呢對戀人毫不羞恥地喺尼努斯墓相會,喺嗰度求愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個人,帶著燈籠、狗和荊棘叢,扮演月光,因為,如果你們想知道,就是在月光下,這對戀人毫不羞恥地在尼努斯墓相會,在那裡求愛。

passages.original: This grisly beast (which Lion hight by name) The trusty Thisbe, coming first by night, Did scare away, or rather did affright;
passages.vernacular: 呢隻可怕嘅野獸(名叫獅子),忠實嘅提斯柏先到夜裡,被牠嚇跑,或者講驚嚇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這隻可怕的野獸(名叫獅子),忠實的提斯柏先到夜裡,被牠嚇跑,或者說驚嚇;

passages.original: And as she fled, her mantle she did fall; Which Lion vile with bloody mouth did stain.
passages.vernacular: 佢逃跑時掉咗斗篷;可惡嘅獅子用血口弄髒咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她逃跑時掉了斗篷;可惡的獅子用血口弄髒了它。

passages.original: Anon comes Pyramus, sweet youth, and tall, And finds his trusty Thisbe’s mantle slain;
passages.vernacular: 不久嚟咗皮拉姆斯,甜美而高大嘅青年,發現佢忠實嘅提斯柏嘅斗篷被殺(染血);
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久來了皮拉姆斯,甜美而高大的青年,發現他忠實的提斯柏的斗篷被殺(染血);

passages.original: Whereat with blade, with bloody blameful blade, He bravely broach’d his boiling bloody breast;
passages.vernacular: 於是佢用劍,用帶血嘅、該受責備嘅劍,勇敢地刺進佢沸騰嘅流血嘅胸膛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他用劍,用帶血的、該受責備的劍,勇敢地刺進他沸騰的流血的胸膛;

passages.original: And Thisbe, tarrying in mulberry shade, His dagger drew, and died.
passages.vernacular: 而提斯柏,喺桑樹蔭下等待,拔出佢嘅匕首,死去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而提斯柏,在桑樹蔭下等待,拔出他的匕首,死去。

passages.original: For all the rest, Let Lion, Moonshine, Wall, and lovers twain, At large discourse while here they do remain.
passages.vernacular: 至於其餘嘅,就讓獅子、月光、牆同兩個戀人,喺呢度逗留時詳細講述。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於其餘的,就讓獅子、月光、牆和兩個戀人,在這裡逗留時詳細講述。

passages.original: [Exeunt Prologue, Pyramus, Thisbe, Lion and Moonshine.]
passages.vernacular: [序幕者、皮拉姆斯、提斯柏、獅子同月光下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [序幕者、皮拉姆斯、提斯柏、獅子與月光下。]

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: I wonder if the lion be to speak.
passages.vernacular: 我奇怪獅子會唔會講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我奇怪獅子會不會說話。

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: No wonder, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 不奇怪,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不奇怪,大人。

passages.original: One lion may, when many asses do.
passages.vernacular: 一頭獅子可以,當許多驢子都可以時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一頭獅子可以,當許多驢子都可以時。

passages.title: Wall 牆
passages.original: In this same interlude it doth befall That I, one Snout by name, present a wall:
passages.vernacular: 喺呢場插劇中,恰好係我,一個叫斯諾特嘅,扮演一堵牆:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這場插劇中,恰好是我,一個叫斯諾特的,扮演一堵牆:

passages.original: And such a wall as I would have you think That had in it a crannied hole or chink, Through which the lovers, Pyramus and Thisbe, Did whisper often very secretly.
passages.vernacular: 一堵我希望你哋認為有裂縫洞或縫隙嘅牆,戀人皮拉姆斯同提斯柏常透過佢好秘密地低聲講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一堵我希望你們認為有裂縫洞或縫隙的牆,戀人皮拉姆斯和提斯柏常透過它非常秘密地低聲說話。

passages.original: This loam, this rough-cast, and this stone, doth show That I am that same wall;
passages.vernacular: 呢黏土、呢粗灰漿同呢石頭,顯示我就係嗰堵牆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這黏土、這粗灰漿和這石頭,顯示我就是那堵牆;

passages.original: the truth is so: And this the cranny is, right and sinister, Through which the fearful lovers are to whisper.
passages.vernacular: 事實就係咁樣:呢個就係嗰裂縫,右邊同左邊,膽怯嘅戀人哋就要透過佢低語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實就是這樣:這就是那裂縫,右邊和左邊,膽怯的戀人們就要透過它低語。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Would you desire lime and hair to speak better?
passages.vernacular: 你想要石灰同毛髮講得更好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想要石灰和毛髮說得更好嗎?

passages.title: Demetrius 狄米特律斯
passages.original: It is the wittiest partition that ever I heard discourse, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我聽過最機智嘅隔板談話,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我聽過最機智的隔板談話,大人。

passages.title: Theseus 忒修斯
passages.original: Pyramus draws near the wall; silence.
passages.vernacular: 皮拉姆斯走近牆;安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮拉姆斯走近牆;安靜。

passages.original: Enter Pyramus.
passages.vernacular: [皮拉姆斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [皮拉姆斯上。]

passages.title: Pyramus 皮拉姆斯
passages.original: O grim-look’d night!
passages.vernacular: 啊,面目猙獰嘅夜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,面目猙獰的夜!

passages.original: O night with hue so black!
passages.vernacular: 啊黑色咁深嘅夜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊黑色這麼深的夜!

passages.original: O night, which ever art when day is not!
passages.vernacular: 啊夜,只要唔係白天你就存在!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊夜,只要不是白天你就存在!

passages.original: O night, O night, alack, alack, alack, I fear my Thisbe’s promise is forgot!
passages.vernacular: 啊夜,啊夜,哎呀,哎呀,哎呀,我怕我嘅提斯柏嘅承諾被忘喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊夜,啊夜,哎呀,哎呀,哎呀,我怕我的提斯柏的承諾被忘了!

passages.original: And thou, O wall, O sweet, O lovely wall, That stand’st between her father’s ground and mine;
passages.vernacular: 仲有你,啊牆,啊甜美可愛嘅牆,你站喺佢父親嘅地同我嘅地之間;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有你,啊牆,啊甜美可愛的牆,你站在她父親的地和我的地之間;

passages.original: Thou wall, O wall, O sweet and lovely wall, Show me thy chink, to blink through with mine eyne.
passages.vernacular: 你牆,啊牆,啊甜美可愛嘅牆,畀我睇你嘅裂縫,好讓我用眼睛窺睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你牆,啊牆,啊甜美可愛的牆,給我看你的裂縫,好讓我用眼睛窺看。

passages.original: [Wall holds up his fingers.]
passages.vernacular: [牆舉起手指。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [牆舉起手指。]

passages.title: Pyramus 皮拉姆斯
passages.original: Thanks, courteous wall: Jove shield thee well for this!
passages.vernacular: 謝謝,有禮嘅牆:願朱庇特為此好好保佑你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝,有禮的牆:願朱庇特為此好好保佑你!

passages.original: But what see I?
passages.vernacular: 但我睇見乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我看見什麼?

passages.original: No Thisbe do I see.
passages.vernacular: 我冇睇見提斯柏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒看見提斯柏。

passages.original: O wicked wall, through whom I see no bliss, Curs’d be thy stones for thus deceiving me!
passages.vernacular: 啊邪惡嘅牆,透過你我睇唔到幸福,願你嘅石頭被詛咒,咁樣欺騙我!
